scene: 老师没有用计算器，只让他们在心里算。Mental arithmetic is part of the test.

senses.title: The study of numbers
senses.definition: the school subject that teaches adding, subtracting, multiplying and dividing

intro.en: Arithmetic is a Greek compound meaning 'the art of number'.
intro.cn: arithmetic 是希腊语复合词，意为「数的技艺」。

items.en: arithmos meant 'number, count'.
items.cn: arithmos 意为「数、计数」。

items.en: tekhnē meant 'art, skill'.
items.cn: tekhnē 意为「技艺、技能」。

items.en: arithmetike tekhnē was the skill of counting.
items.cn: arithmetike tekhnē 即计数的技艺。

items.en: Latin kept the word as the name of a school subject.
items.cn: 拉丁语把它保留为一门学校科目之名。

items.en: English arithmetic named one of the seven liberal arts.
items.cn: 英语 arithmetic 曾是七艺之一。

note.en: The look-alike group is the same Greek stem; the near-meaning group gives broader or narrower number words.
note.cn: 形近组同出一个希腊词干；近义组是范围更大或更窄的数的词。

definition_zh: n. 舰队（尤指一五八八年西班牙无敌舰队）；一大群同向行进的车船飞机
definition_en: A large fleet of warships, especially the Spanish fleet sent against England; by extension, any large group of vehicles moving together.
core_image: 一整片船帆压过来，数都数不清
scene: 西班牙派出无敌舰队远征英格兰。Spain sent the Armada against England.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armada 指大批战舰组成的舰队，大写 the Armada 特指西班牙无敌舰队。

pos.zh: 舰队；一大群行进的车船

senses.title: A great fleet of warships
senses.definition: a large group of armed ships sailing together, the sense made famous by the Spanish fleet
senses.definitionCN: 一同航行的大批武装船只，因西班牙舰队而闻名
senses.example: The armada stretched along the horizon.
senses.exampleCN: 舰队沿着地平线铺开。
senses.why: The word is built on arms, weapons, so an armada is literally an armed mass, a crowd defined by its weapons.
senses.whyCN: 这个词建在 arms「武器」之上，所以 armada 字面就是「武装起来的一大群」，由武器定义的群体。

senses.title: Any mass moving together
senses.titleCN: 任何一同移动的庞大群体
senses.definition: by extension, a large number of vehicles, boats or aircraft travelling as one body
senses.definitionCN: 引申指作为一个整体行进的大量车辆、船只或飞机
senses.example: An armada of delivery vans filled the narrow lane.
senses.exampleCN: 一大群送货车挤满了那条窄巷。
senses.why: Once the naval picture was fixed, the striking part was the sheer number, so the word spread to any impressive procession.
senses.whyCN: 海军画面固定之后，最醒目的是数量之多，于是这个词扩展到任何气势庞大的行列。

intro.en: Armada is Spanish armada, fleet, from armado, armed, from Latin armata, an armed force, the participle of armare, to arm, from arma, weapons.
intro.cn: armada 就是西班牙语 armada「舰队」，来自 armado「武装的」，而后者出自拉丁语 armata「武装力量」，是 armare「武装」的分词，词根为 arma「武器」。

items.en: Latin arma meant arms or weapons, and also the fittings of a ship, which links weapons and sailing early on.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arma 意为「武器」，也指船上的装备，很早就把武器与航海连在一起。

items.en: The verb armare meant to furnish with weapons, to equip a man or a vessel for fighting.
items.cn: 动词 armare 意为「配备武器」，即为人员或船只装上作战装备。

items.en: Its feminine participle armata came to mean an armed force, the ancestor of army and armada alike.
items.cn: 其阴性分词 armata 转而指「武装力量」，是 army 与 armada 共同的祖先。

items.en: Spanish armada named a fleet, keeping the naval side of arma that other languages dropped.
items.cn: 西班牙语 armada 指舰队，保留了 arma 中其他语言丢掉的航海一面。

items.en: English borrowed armada in the 1530s as a general word for a large fleet of warships.
items.cn: 英语在 1530 年代借入 armada，泛指大批战舰组成的舰队。

items.en: The failed Spanish invasion of 1588 froze the capitalised Armada into English memory as one specific fleet.
items.cn: 1588 年西班牙入侵失败，使大写的 Armada 在英语记忆中定格为那支特定舰队。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the arms family together and adds armadillo, Spanish for the little armed one; the near-meaning group lists words for groups of ships.
note.cn: 形近组把「武器」词族排在一起，并加上 armadillo——西班牙语「披甲的小家伙」；近义组列出表示船群的词。

normalIntro.en: Armada is arm plus the Spanish group ending -ada: an armed mass, which at sea means a fleet.
normalIntro.cn: armada 就是 arm 加西班牙语群体后缀 -ada：武装起来的一大群，在海上就是舰队。

normal.en: Capitalised Armada means the Spanish fleet of 1588.
normal.cn: 大写的 Armada 指 1588 年西班牙舰队。

normal.en: Lower case armada can describe vans or planes.
normal.cn: 小写 armada 可形容送货车或机群。

normal.en: The pattern is an armada of plus a plural noun.
normal.cn: 常见句式是 an armada of 加复数名词。

normal.en: Army is land, armada is sea, both from arma.
normal.cn: army 在陆，armada 在海，都出自 arma。

normal.en: Armadillo is the same Spanish root, little armed one.
normal.cn: armadillo 同源，意为「披甲的小家伙」。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arm「武器」+ -ada「一大群」——武装起来的一整群船，就是舰队 armada。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器、船具」生出 armare「武装」，分词 armata「武装力量」在西班牙语中作 armada「舰队」；1588 年西班牙入侵使大写 Armada 专指那支舰队。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are one armed mass: warships sailing as a body, and any procession whose sheer number makes the same impression.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一群「武装的庞大群体」：作为一个整体航行的战舰，以及任何以数量造成同样印象的行列。

intro.en: Armada is arm plus the Spanish collective ending -ada; the same root builds army, armour, armament and disarm.
intro.cn: armada 是 arm 加西班牙语集合后缀 -ada；同一词根还构成 army、armour、armament 与 disarm。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, weapons, armare, to arm, and armata, an armed force; navis, ship, gives navy beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma「武器」、armare「武装」与 armata「武装力量」；旁边的 navis「船」产生 navy。

definition_zh: n. 军备，武器装备（总称）；（舰船或飞机的）武器系统；武装起来的过程
definition_en: The weapons and military resources of a country or force; the guns and missile systems fitted to a ship or aircraft; the process of arming for war.
core_image: 把武器一件件装到船上、机上、国库里
scene: 条约限制重型军备的部署。The treaty limits the deployment of heavy armament.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armament 指一国或一支力量的武器与军力总称。

senses.title: A country's military resources
senses.definition: the whole stock of weapons, vehicles and equipment a state or force maintains
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家或一支武装力量所维持的全部武器、载具与装备
senses.example: The report compares the armament of the two alliances.
senses.exampleCN: 报告比较了两大同盟的军备。
senses.why: The suffix -ment names means or result, so armament is what arming produces: the equipment itself.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 表手段或结果，所以 armament 就是「武装」所产出的东西：装备本身。

senses.title: The guns fitted to a vessel
senses.definition: the specific guns, cannon or missile systems mounted on a ship, aircraft or vehicle
senses.definitionCN: 安装在舰船、飞机或车辆上的具体火炮、舰炮或导弹系统
senses.example: The cruiser's main armament was removed after the war.
senses.exampleCN: 这艘巡洋舰的主炮系统在战后被拆除。
senses.why: Here the word narrows from a nation to one hull: the same equipping idea applied to a single platform.
senses.whyCN: 这里词义从一国收窄到一条船：同样的「装备」概念用在单个平台上。

senses.title: The act of arming
senses.definition: the process of building up military strength, the sense behind armament race
senses.definitionCN: 扩充军力的过程，即 armament race 背后的含义
senses.example: Rapid armament followed the breakdown of talks.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判破裂之后迅速展开了军备扩充。
senses.why: Because -ment can name an action as well as its result, the word also covers the building up, not only the stock.
senses.whyCN: 因为 -ment 既可表结果也可表动作，这个词也涵盖「扩充」本身，而不只是存量。

intro.en: Armament is Latin armamentum, equipment, from armare, to arm, plus the means suffix -mentum. English first used it for the guns of a warship.
intro.cn: armament 就是拉丁语 armamentum「装备」，由 armare「武装」加表手段的后缀 -mentum 构成。英语最初用它指战舰的火炮。

items.en: Latin arma meant weapons and gear, the base of arm, army, armour and armada.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arma 意为武器与装备，是 arm、army、armour 与 armada 的共同基础。

items.en: Armare meant to equip for fighting, whether a soldier, a ship or a fortress.
items.cn: armare 意为「为作战而装备」，对象可以是士兵、船只或堡垒。

items.en: Adding -mentum, the suffix for a means or instrument, gave armamentum, the equipment itself.
items.cn: 加上表手段或工具的后缀 -mentum 得到 armamentum，即装备本身。

items.en: English recorded armament in the 1690s for the guns carried by a warship.
items.cn: 英语在 1690 年代记录 armament，指战舰所携火炮。

items.en: Through the eighteenth century the word widened from one ship's guns to a whole state's military stock.
items.cn: 整个 18 世纪，词义从一条船的火炮扩展到一国全部的军事存量。

items.en: Twentieth-century treaties made armament and disarmament standard terms of international law.
items.cn: 20 世纪的条约使 armament 与 disarmament 成为国际法的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group contrasts armistice, a stop to fighting, with armament, the means of it; the near-meaning group lists other words for weapons.
note.cn: 形近组把 armistice「停战」与 armament「作战手段」对照；近义组列出其他表示武器的词。

examples.cn: 以吨位而言，这艘船的武器配置不算多。

examples.en: Both sides pledged to cut their armaments.
examples.cn: 双方承诺削减各自军备。

examples.en: The treaty froze further armament in the region.
examples.cn: 条约冻结了该地区的进一步军备扩充。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arm「武器」+ -ment「手段、结果」——武装出来的装备，就是军备 armament。

root: 拉丁语 arma「武器」生出 armare「武装」，加表手段的后缀 -mentum 成 armamentum「装备」；英语 1690 年代先指舰炮，后扩展为一国军备。

sensesIntro.en: The three senses follow one equipping: the stock a nation holds, the guns on one hull, and the act of building the stock up.
sensesIntro.cn: 三个义项沿着同一次「装备」展开：一国持有的存量、一条船上的火炮，以及把存量堆起来的过程。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: weapons being fitted one by one onto ships, planes and into stores

intro.en: Armament is arm plus -ment, and with dis- it flips to disarm and disarmament; the root also builds armour and army.
intro.cn: armament 是 arm 加 -ment，加上 dis- 就翻转为 disarm 与 disarmament；同一词根还构成 armour 与 army。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is arma, armare and armamentum; -mentum is the Latin suffix for a means or instrument.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 arma、armare 与 armamentum；-mentum 是拉丁语表手段或工具的后缀。

definition_zh: n. 军械库，武器库（美式拼作 armory）；（引申）可动用的手段总和
definition_en: A place where weapons are stored or made; by extension, the whole range of resources or arguments someone can draw on. American English spells it armory.
core_image: 一屋子挂满兵器，随时可以取用
scene: 城堡的军械库里挂满了长矛。The castle armoury was lined with spears.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：armoury 指存放或制造武器的库房，美式拼写为 armory。

pos.zh: 军械库；武器库；手段总和

senses.title: A store of weapons
senses.definition: a room or building where arms are kept, and sometimes where they are manufactured
senses.definitionCN: 存放武器的房间或建筑，有时也指制造武器的场所
senses.example: The rebels seized the armoury before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 叛军在黎明前夺下了军械库。
senses.why: The Latin base is a chest or cupboard, so armoury is literally the cupboard for arms, a place defined by what it holds.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语底层是「柜子」，所以 armoury 字面就是「放武器的柜子」，一个由所存之物定义的场所。

senses.title: The range you can draw on
senses.definition: figuratively, the full set of skills, arguments or measures available to a person
senses.definitionCN: 比喻义，指一个人可动用的全部技能、论据或措施
senses.example: Patience is the strongest weapon in her armoury.
senses.exampleCN: 耐心是她手段中最有力的一件。
senses.why: The store image transfers neatly: skills sit ready on the wall like weapons, waiting to be taken down.
senses.whyCN: 库房的画面顺畅地转移过来：技能像武器一样挂在墙上待取。

intro.en: Armoury comes from Latin armarium, a chest or closet, from arma, weapons. Old French armoire kept the cupboard sense, while English specialised it to arms.
intro.cn: armoury 来自拉丁语 armarium「柜子、壁橱」，词根为 arma「武器」。古法语 armoire 保留「柜子」义，英语则把它专指武器存放处。

items.en: Arma meant weapons and gear, the base shared by arm, army, armour and armada.
items.cn: arma 意为武器与装备，是 arm、army、armour 与 armada 共有的词根。

items.en: Armarium named a chest or closet, originally for arms but later for books and valuables.
items.cn: armarium 指柜子或壁橱，最初放武器，后来也放书与贵重物品。

items.en: Old French armoire kept the furniture sense, which is why French armoire still means a wardrobe.
items.cn: 古法语 armoire 保留家具义，因此法语 armoire 至今仍指大衣柜。

items.en: English took the word for a place where arms are stored, narrowing the cupboard to weapons.
items.cn: 英语用这个词指存放武器的地方，把「柜子」收窄为武器。

items.en: Nineteenth-century writers began calling a person's stock of arguments their armoury.
items.cn: 19 世纪作者开始把一个人掌握的论据称为他的 armoury。

items.en: American reform dropped the u to give armory, while British usage kept armoury.

definition_zh: n. 唤起，激起（兴趣、情绪、注意）；（生理与心理学）唤醒状态，兴奋水平
definition_en: The act of stirring a feeling, interest or response into activity; in psychology and physiology, the level of alertness and activation of the body.
core_image: 把睡着的那根弦一下拨响
scene: 咖啡因提高了警觉与生理唤醒水平。Caffeine raises alertness and physiological arousal.
sceneCN: 第 2 个义项：在心理学与生理学中，arousal 指身体的唤醒与激活水平。

senses.title: Stirring a feeling into activity
senses.definition: the act of waking interest, anger, curiosity or desire so that it becomes active
senses.definitionCN: 把兴趣、愤怒、好奇或欲望唤醒，使之变为活跃状态的行为
senses.example: The photograph caused widespread arousal of public anger.
senses.exampleCN: 那张照片激起了公众普遍的愤怒。
senses.why: The verb arouse meant to shake a bird into flight, so the noun keeps that sudden start from stillness.
senses.whyCN: 动词 arouse 原意是把鸟惊飞，所以这个名词保留着「从静止中猛然启动」的画面。

senses.title: The body's activation level
senses.definition: in psychology and physiology, a measurable state of alertness ranging from deep sleep to high excitement
senses.definitionCN: 在心理学与生理学中，指从深睡到高度兴奋之间可测量的警觉状态
senses.example: Performance drops when arousal is either too low or too high.
senses.exampleCN: 唤醒水平过低或过高，表现都会下降。
senses.why: Science needed a neutral word for how switched on the body is, and arousal supplied it without judging the feeling.
senses.whyCN: 科学需要一个中性词来描述身体「开机」的程度，arousal 恰好胜任，且不对感受作评价。

intro.en: Arousal is arouse plus the action suffix -al. Rouse comes from Middle English rousen, to shake, originally a falconry term for making a hawk stir its feathers.
intro.cn: arousal 是 arouse 加动作名词后缀 -al。rouse 来自中古英语 rousen「抖动」，原本是鹰猎术语，指让鹰抖动羽毛。

items.en: Middle English rousen meant to shake or startle, used of birds and of sleeping people alike.
items.cn: 中古英语 rousen 意为「抖动、惊动」，既用于鸟，也用于睡着的人。

items.en: In falconry a hawk was roused when it shook its feathers and became alert, the image behind the whole family.
items.cn: 鹰猎中，鹰抖动羽毛转为警觉称为 roused，这是整个词族背后的画面。

items.en: English added the intensive prefix a- to give arouse, to stir up thoroughly, by the sixteenth century.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪，英语加上强调前缀 a- 得到 arouse，意为「彻底激起」。

items.en: The action noun arousal is recorded in 1849, formed with -al as in arrival and refusal.
items.cn: 动作名词 arousal 记录于 1849 年，用 -al 构成，与 arrival、refusal 同型。

items.en: Early twentieth-century psychology adopted arousal for the body's activation level, giving arousal theory.
items.cn: 20 世纪初心理学采用 arousal 指身体激活水平，产生了唤醒理论。

items.en: Today arousal is standard in sleep research, emotion studies and sports science.
items.cn: 如今 arousal 是睡眠研究、情绪研究与运动科学的标准用语。

note.en: The look-alike group warns against carousal, a noisy drinking party, which differs by one letter; the near-meaning group lists words for being stirred up.
note.cn: 形近组提醒别与只差一个字母的 carousal「喧闹酒宴」混淆；近义组列出表示被激起的词。

definition_zh: 唤起；激起；唤醒；引起
definition_en: to cause a feeling or reaction to appear, or to wake someone
core_image: 轻轻一推，让沉睡的东西动起来
scene: 台下的人原本昏昏欲睡。The speaker aroused their interest with a single question.
sceneCN: 这里 arouse 是「激起」（第 1 个义项：使某种情绪或反应产生）；句意是演讲者用一个问题激起了他们的兴趣。

senses.title: To stir up a feeling
senses.definition: to make an emotion or reaction begin to exist
senses.definitionCN: 使某种情绪或反应开始存在
senses.example: The speaker aroused their interest with a single question.
senses.exampleCN: 演讲者用一个问题激起了他们的兴趣。
senses.why: Rouse meant to shake someone awake; arouse adds the idea of setting a feeling in motion.
senses.whyCN: rouse 意为把人摇醒；arouse 则添上「让某种情绪动起来」的意思。

senses.title: To wake someone
senses.definition: to bring a sleeping person back to waking
senses.definitionCN: 使睡着的人回到清醒状态
senses.example: The noise aroused him from a deep sleep.
senses.exampleCN: 那声响把他从沉睡中唤醒。
senses.why: This is the older physical sense, still used when the waking is gentle or slightly literary.
senses.whyCN: 这是更早的身体义，在语气温和或略偏书面时仍在使用。

senses.title: To provoke a hostile reaction
senses.definition: to cause suspicion, anger, or criticism
senses.definitionCN: 引起怀疑、愤怒或批评
senses.example: His sudden wealth aroused suspicion.
senses.exampleCN: 他的突然暴富引起了怀疑。
senses.why: Once the word could start any feeling, it naturally covered unpleasant ones such as doubt and anger.
senses.whyCN: 既然这个词能启动任何情绪，自然也涵盖怀疑、愤怒这类不快的情绪。

intro.en: Arouse is a- 'up' added to the older verb rouse.

items.en: Feelings and suspicions became its commonest objects.

definition_zh: 安排；筹备；排列；整理
definition_en: to plan and organise something, or to put things in a particular order
core_image: 把散乱的东西一件件摆成一行
scene: 桌上摊着十几份文件，他一份份摆好。She arranged the papers into three neat piles.
sceneCN: 这里 arrange 是「整理排列」（第 2 个义项：把东西按顺序摆好）；句意是她把文件理成了三摞整齐的纸。

senses.title: To plan an event
senses.definition: to make the necessary plans for something to happen
senses.definitionCN: 为使某事发生而做好必要准备
senses.example: I have arranged a meeting for Monday morning.
senses.exampleCN: 我已安排在周一上午开个会。
senses.why: Old French arengier meant 'to put in a row', and a row of steps in time is what a plan is.
senses.whyCN: 古法语 arengier 意为「排成一行」，而把步骤按时间排成一行，就是计划。

senses.title: To put in order
senses.definition: to place things in a chosen order or pattern
senses.definitionCN: 把物品按选定的顺序或样式摆放
senses.example: She arranged the papers into three neat piles.
senses.exampleCN: 她把文件理成了三摞整齐的纸。
senses.why: This is the literal row sense: objects are ranged so that their places make sense.
senses.whyCN: 这是字面上的「成行」义：物品被排好，使各自的位置合于秩序。

senses.title: To come to an agreement about
senses.definition: to settle details with someone in advance
senses.definitionCN: 事先与某人把细节谈定
senses.example: We arranged for a taxi to meet us at the airport.
senses.exampleCN: 我们安排了一辆出租车到机场接我们。
senses.why: Planning something with another person requires agreeing on the order of events, hence the sense of settling.
senses.whyCN: 与别人一起计划某事，必须先就事情的次序达成一致，于是产生「谈妥」义。

senses.why: This is the noun at its most literal: the visible result of having ranged objects into places.
senses.whyCN: 这是该名词最字面的用法：把物品排到各自位置之后可见的结果。

senses.title: A settled agreement
senses.definition: an understanding reached between two sides
senses.definitionCN: 双方之间达成的谅解
senses.example: They have an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
senses.exampleCN: 他们和房东之间有关于房租的约定。
senses.why: When the rows being ordered are other people's interests, the result is a deal rather than a layout.
senses.whyCN: 当被排列的是彼此的利益时，排出来的结果就不是布置，而是协议。

intro.en: Arrangement is the noun of arrange, from a French verb of setting in rows.
intro.cn: arrangement 是 arrange 的名词，后者来自一个「排成行」的法语动词。

items.en: rang meant 'row, line, rank'.
items.cn: rang 意为「行、列、排」。

items.en: arengier meant 'to set in a row'.
items.cn: arengier 意为「排成一行」。

items.en: English arrange kept the ordering sense.
items.cn: 英语 arrange 保留了排列义。

items.en: arrangement added the sense of a settled plan.
items.cn: arrangement 又添上「议定的方案」一义。

items.en: The word now covers layout, preparations, and agreements.
items.cn: 如今它涵盖布置、筹备与约定三层意思。

note.en: The look-alike group is the arrange family; the near-meaning group gives plan, layout, and deal.
note.cn: 形近组是 arrange 词族；近义组分别给出计划、布局与协议。

entries.definition: to plan or order
put in order
to order again
a set of intended steps
the way parts are placed
a shared understanding

normalIntro.en: An arrangement is a row that has been decided on.
normalIntro.cn: arrangement 就是已经定下来的那一行排列。

normal.en: Make arrangements is the plural idiom for preparing.
normal.cn: make arrangements 是表示筹备的复数习语。

normal.en: A seating arrangement describes who sits where.
normal.cn: seating arrangement 描述谁坐哪儿。

normal.en: By arrangement means after agreeing with someone.
normal.cn: by arrangement 意为经与某人商定。

normal.en: The stress falls on the second syllable.
normal.cn: 重音落在第二个音节。

normal.en: The verb behind it is arrange.
normal.cn: 其背后的动词是 arrange。

abstract.en: See name cards placed on a long table.
abstract.cn: 想象长桌上摆好的名牌。

abstract.en: See a list of steps ticked off.
abstract.cn: 想象一串步骤被逐条勾掉。

abstract.en: See two hands shaking over a paper.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手在纸上方相握。

examples.en: All the travel arrangements are in place.
examples.cn: 所有出行安排都已就绪。

examples.en: The seating arrangement was changed twice.
examples.cn: 座位安排改过两次。

examples.en: They have an arrangement with the landlord about the rent.
examples.cn: 他们和房东之间有关于房租的约定。

dict_mnemonic.text: arrange（排列）加 -ment：排列出来的结果，就是布置；排好的步骤，就是安排。

root: 由动词 arrange 加名词后缀 -ment 构成；arrange 源自古法语 arengier「排成一行」，词根 rang 意为行列。

sensesIntro.en: Rows of objects give a layout, rows of steps give a plan, and rows of interests give a deal.
sensesIntro.cn: 物品排成行给出布置，步骤排成行给出计划，利益排成行给出协议。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: every object on a table sitting in its appointed place.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上每件东西都待在指定的位置。

intro.en: A noun of ordering that grew a sense of agreement.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示排序的名词，后来长出「协议」义。

latinIntro.en: The row stem rang also gives range and rank.
latinIntro.cn: 行列词干 rang 也派生出 range 与 rank。

definition_zh: n. 一大批（整齐摆开之物）；阵列；数组；战斗队列；v. 排列；部署
definition_en: An ordered or impressive collection of things set out in rows; in computing, a block of values reached by an index; a battle formation; as a verb, to arrange or deploy in order.
core_image: 东西一件件排成行，一眼望过去整整齐齐
scene: 桌上摆开了一整排样品。An array of samples was laid out on the table.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：array 指按顺序摆开的一大批东西，最常见的句式是 an array of。

collocations.zh: 令人眼花缭乱的一大排

senses.title: An ordered collection on display
senses.definition: a large group of things set out in an ordered or impressive way, the commonest modern use
senses.definitionCN: 按顺序或气势摆开的一大群东西，是现代最常见的用法
senses.example: The shop offers a wide array of cheeses.
senses.exampleCN: 这家店摆出各式各样的奶酪。
senses.why: The verb first meant to draw up troops in order, so the noun kept the picture of rows even when the rows held food instead of soldiers.
senses.whyCN: 动词最初指把部队列成阵，所以名词即便摆的是食物而不是士兵，也保留了「成行」的画面。

senses.title: Battle formation
senses.definition: troops drawn up in order for fighting, the oldest sense of the noun
senses.definitionCN: 为作战而列成阵的部队，是名词最古老的义项
senses.example: The general arrayed his men along the ridge.
senses.exampleCN: 将军把士兵沿山脊列成阵。
senses.why: This is the source sense: order before battle was survival, which is why the same root also gave ready.
senses.whyCN: 这是源头义项：战前的秩序意味着生存，所以同一词根还给出了 ready「准备好的」。

senses.title: A block of values in computing
senses.definition: a set of values stored together under one name and reached by a numbered position
senses.definitionCN: 存在同一个名字下、按编号位置取用的一组数值
senses.example: The program stores the readings in an array.
senses.exampleCN: 程序把读数存进一个数组。
senses.why: Early programmers needed a word for values sitting side by side in memory, and the old row picture fitted exactly.
senses.whyCN: 早期程序员需要一个词来称呼在内存里并排放着的数值，古老的「成行」画面正好贴合。

senses.title: To arrange or deploy
senses.definition: to place people or things in a deliberate order, especially for a purpose
senses.definitionCN: 把人员或物品按某种意图摆成次序，尤指为某个目的
senses.example: Nurses arrayed the instruments on the tray.
senses.exampleCN: 护士把器械在托盘上依次摆好。
senses.why: The verb never lost its sense of purpose: you array things for use or for show, never at random.
senses.whyCN: 动词始终带着「有目的」的意味：array 是为了使用或展示而摆，绝不是随手乱放。

intro.en: Array comes from Old French areer, to put in order, from rei, order, itself from a Frankish word for ready; the same root gives English ready.
intro.cn: array 来自古法语 areer「整理、列队」，其词源是 rei「次序」，再往上是法兰克语中表示「准备好」的词；同一词根还给出英语 ready。

items.en: A Frankish word meaning ready or prepared lies behind both ready and array, a rare Germanic root in a French-looking word.
items.cn: 一个意为「准备好」的法兰克语词同时藏在 ready 与 array 背后，是这个看似法语的词里少见的日耳曼词根。

items.en: Old French rei meant order or arrangement, the noun from which the verb was built.
items.cn: 古法语 rei 意为「次序、安排」，是构成动词的名词基础。

items.en: The verb areer meant to put in order or prepare, and especially to draw up troops for battle.
items.cn: 动词 areer 意为「整理、准备」，尤指为作战把部队列成阵。

items.en: Middle English arayen meant to dress, equip or draw up in order, and the noun aray named the order itself.
items.cn: 中古英语 arayen 意为「装束、装备、列队」，名词 aray 则指那份次序本身。

items.en: By the fifteenth century the noun could name any impressive ordered collection, not only lines of soldiers.
items.cn: 到十五世纪，名词已可指任何气势可观的有序集合，不再限于士兵的行列。

items.en: Early programmers took array for a block of values reached by an index, keeping the row picture intact.
items.cn: 早期程序员用 array 指按索引取用的一组数值，完整保留了「成行」的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group separates array from ray, arraign and arrange, and adds its own opposite disarray; the near-meaning group lists words for collections.
note.cn: 形近组把 array 与 ray、arraign、arrange 分开，并加上它自己的反义词 disarray；近义组列出表示「一批东西」的词。

entries.definition: A narrow beam of light or energy.
entries.definitionCN: 一道细窄的光线或能量。

entries.definition: To call someone before a court to answer a charge.
entries.definitionCN: 传唤某人上法庭答辩指控。

entries.definition: To put things in a chosen order.
entries.definitionCN: 把东西按选定的次序摆放。

entries.definition: A state of disorder and confusion.
A mixed collection of different things.
entries.definitionCN: 各式各样东西的混合集合。

entries.definition: The whole span of things available.
Things set out so that they can be seen.
entries.definitionCN: 摆出来供人观看的东西。

entries.definition: A group chosen from a larger set.
entries.definitionCN: 从更大集合中挑出的一组。

normalIntro.en: Array comes from a word for putting in order, so every sense keeps one picture: things standing in rows.
normalIntro.cn: array 出自一个表示「整理成序」的词，所以每个义项都保留同一幅画面：东西排成行。

normal.en: The everyday pattern is an array of plus a plural noun.
normal.cn: 日常句式是 an array of 加复数名词。

normal.en: Soldiers, cheeses and numbers all sit in an array.
normal.cn: 士兵、奶酪和数值都可以摆成 array。

normal.en: Arrayed and arraying are the verb forms.
normal.cn: 动词形式是 arrayed 与 arraying。

normal.en: Disarray is the same word turned upside down.
normal.cn: disarray 是同一个词翻了个面。

normal.en: Ready and address share the old root of order.
normal.cn: ready 与 address 共用「次序」这个古词根。

abstract.en: Picture bottles standing in a straight line by height.
abstract.cn: 想象瓶子按高矮排成一条直线。

abstract.en: Imagine soldiers drawn up along a ridge before a fight.
abstract.cn: 想象开战前沿山脊列阵的士兵。

abstract.en: Think of numbered boxes sitting side by side in memory.
abstract.cn: 想象内存里并排放着的带编号的格子。

examples.en: The buffet offered an array of hot dishes.
examples.cn: 自助餐摆出一大排热菜。

examples.en: She arrayed the bottles by height.
examples.cn: 她把瓶子按高矮排好。

examples.en: Each sensor value sits in an array.
examples.cn: 每个传感器读数都存在数组里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：array 听着像 a + ray「一道光线」——光线笔直地排开，正是一列列摆好的东西，array。

root: 法兰克语中表示「准备好」的词经古法语 rei「次序」与 areer「整理、列队」进入中古英语 arayen；同一词根还给出 ready 与 address，本义始终是「排成行」。

sensesIntro.en: All four senses are one act of ordering: soldiers drawn up, goods set out, values stored side by side, and the verb that does the arranging.
sensesIntro.cn: 四个义项是同一个「排成序」的动作：列阵的士兵、摆开的货品、并排存放的数值，以及执行摆放的那个动词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: things standing one after another in tidy rows
core.cn: 核心意象：东西一件件排成行，整整齐齐

branches.en: Troops drawn up along a ridge.
Instruments placed in order on a tray.
branches.cn: 在托盘上依次摆好的器械。

branches.en: A wide spread of cheeses on a counter.
branches.cn: 柜台上摆开的一大排奶酪。

branches.en: Numbered values sitting side by side.
branches.cn: 并排放着的带编号的数值。

branches.en: Order imposed for a purpose, never at random.
branches.cn: 为某个目的排出的次序，绝非随手乱放。

intro.en: Array carries the Old French prefix a-, to, and lives among the ordering suffixes -ment, -ion, -ness and -ed.
intro.cn: array 带着古法语前缀 a-「朝向」，周围是表示次序的后缀 -ment、-ion、-ness 与 -ed。

latinIntro.en: Array is Germanic in origin, but Latin ordo, order, and ordinare, to arrange, supply the surrounding vocabulary of rows.
latinIntro.cn: array 本属日耳曼语来源，但拉丁语 ordo「次序」与 ordinare「排列」提供了周边关于「行」的词汇。

latinEntries.exampleCN: ordo 产生 order 与 ordinal。
ordinare 产生 ordain 与 ordinate。

latinEntries.meaning: a row of things joined together
latinEntries.example: Series names a line of items.
latinEntries.exampleCN: series 指一列相连的条目。

definition_zh: n. 傲慢；自大；（对权力或知识的）越界自信
definition_en: An exaggerated sense of your own importance shown in dismissive behaviour towards others; overreaching confidence, as in the arrogance of power.
core_image: 下巴抬得比谁都高，别人的话一句也听不进
scene: 他的傲慢让全队都不愿开口。His arrogance silenced the whole team.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arrogance 指自视过高、看不起别人的态度。

senses.title: A superior attitude towards others
senses.definition: a manner that treats other people as less important or less able than yourself
senses.definitionCN: 把别人看得不如自己重要、不如自己能干的态度
senses.example: Her arrogance made junior staff afraid to speak.
senses.exampleCN: 她的傲慢让年轻员工不敢开口。
senses.why: The root means to ask for oneself, so the word describes someone who keeps claiming more standing than others are given.
senses.whyCN: 词根意为「为自己索取」，所以这个词描述的是不断为自己索要地位、却不给别人留位置的人。

senses.title: Overreaching confidence
senses.definition: confidence that claims more authority or knowledge than it has earned, as in the arrogance of power
senses.definitionCN: 声称拥有超出实际所得的权威或知识的自信，如「权力的傲慢」
senses.example: The report warns against the arrogance of power.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告警告人们警惕权力的傲慢。
senses.why: Political writing widened the word from personal manners to whole institutions that assume they cannot be wrong.
senses.whyCN: 政治评论把这个词从个人举止扩展到整个机构——那些自认不会出错的机构。

intro.en: Arrogance is Latin arrogantia, from arrogare, to claim for oneself, formed from ad, to, plus rogare, to ask: asking for more than your share.
intro.cn: arrogance 就是拉丁语 arrogantia，出自 arrogare「为自己索取」，由 ad「向」加 rogare「问」构成：索要超过本分的东西。

items.en: Latin rogare meant to ask, and also to propose a law, so asking carried public weight rather than private pleading.
items.cn: 拉丁语 rogare 意为「问」，也指「提出法案」，因此「问」带着公共分量，而非私下请求。

items.en: With ad, to, the verb arrogare meant to ask for oneself, to claim what was not properly yours.
items.cn: 加上 ad「向」之后，动词 arrogare 意为「为自己索取」，即把本不属于自己的东西据为己有。

items.en: The participle arrogans described someone claiming too much, presumptuous rather than merely proud.
items.cn: 分词 arrogans 描述索求过度的人，重点在「僭越」而不只是「骄傲」。

items.en: The noun arrogantia named that settled habit of claiming more than one deserved.
items.cn: 名词 arrogantia 指那种惯常的、索求超出本分的习性。

items.en: English took arrogance through French in the fourteenth century, alongside the adjective arrogant.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪经法语借入 arrogance，同时带入形容词 arrogant。

items.en: Twentieth-century political writing fixed phrases such as the arrogance of power, widening the word beyond personal manners.
items.cn: 二十世纪政治评论固定了「权力的傲慢」这类说法，把这个词从个人举止推向更广的范围。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the asking root together and adds two words that merely share the ending -ance; the near-meaning group grades pride from mild to dangerous.
note.cn: 形近组把「索取」词根排在一起，并加上两个只是共用 -ance 结尾的词；近义组按程度从轻到危排列各种「自负」。

entries.definition: Showing too high a view of yourself.
To claim a right without justification.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无依据地把权利据为己有。

entries.definition: Lack of knowledge or awareness.
Graceful refinement of style.
Too high an opinion of your own ability.
Proud coldness towards other people.
Overconfidence that invites a downfall.
Taking liberties you have no right to take.

normalIntro.en: Arrogance is ad plus rogare, to ask: asking for more than your share until you treat others as beneath you.
normalIntro.cn: arrogance 就是 ad 加 rogare「问」：不断索要超出本分的东西，直到把别人看成低自己一等。

normal.en: Arrogance is the noun, arrogant the adjective.
normal.cn: arrogance 是名词，arrogant 是形容词。

normal.en: Arrogate keeps the older sense, to claim a right.
normal.cn: arrogate 保留古义「僭取权利」。

normal.en: Ignorance ends the same way but comes from not knowing.
normal.cn: ignorance 结尾相同，却来自「不知道」。

normal.en: Common patterns are sheer arrogance and the arrogance of power.
normal.cn: 常见搭配是 sheer arrogance 与 the arrogance of power。

normal.en: Arrogance is uncountable, so no plural is used.
normal.cn: arrogance 不可数，因此不用复数。

abstract.en: Picture a chin lifted so high that no advice gets in.
abstract.cn: 想象下巴抬得太高，任何建议都进不去。

abstract.en: Imagine a meeting where one voice fills the whole room.
abstract.cn: 想象一场会议被一个人的声音占满。

abstract.en: Think of a hand reaching past its own plate.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手伸过了自己那份盘子。

examples.en: His arrogance cost him the team.
examples.cn: 他的傲慢让他失去了整个团队。

examples.en: Sheer arrogance blinded the board to the risk.
examples.cn: 十足的傲慢让董事会看不见风险。

examples.en: They spoke of the arrogance of power.
examples.cn: 他们谈到权力的傲慢。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：ar-「向」+ rog「问」+ -ance「状态」——开口就为自己索取，索取得多了便成了傲慢 arrogance。

root: 拉丁语 rogare「问、提议」加 ad-「向」构成 arrogare「为自己索取」，分词 arrogans「僭取的」生出 arrogantia；十四世纪经法语入英语，本义是「索取超过本分」。

sensesIntro.en: Both senses are the same reach past your own share: one aimed at people, the other at authority and knowledge.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项都是同一种「伸过本分」的手：一个指向他人，一个指向权威与知识。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chin lifted so high that no other voice gets in
core.cn: 核心意象：下巴抬得极高，别人的声音一句也进不来

branches.en: A chin lifted above everyone else.
Power that assumes it cannot be wrong.

branches.cn: 超出证据范围的自我权威。

branches.en: Both claim more than one has earned.
branches.cn: 两者都索取超出自己应得的东西。

intro.en: Arrogance is ar- from ad-, to, plus rog-, ask, plus -ance; the same asking root builds interrogate and prerogative.
intro.cn: arrogance 由 ad- 变来的 ar-「向」加 rog-「问」再加 -ance 构成；同一「问」词根还构成 interrogate 与 prerogative。

latinIntro.en: The Latin layer is rogare, to ask, arrogare, to claim for oneself, and arrogantia, the habit of claiming too much.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语层次是 rogare「问」、arrogare「为自己索取」与 arrogantia「索求过度的习性」。

latinEntries.meaning: to ask, to propose a law

latinEntries.exampleCN: arrogare 产生 arrogate 与 arrogant。

latinEntries.meaning: the habit of claiming too much

definition_zh: 傲慢的；自大的；狂妄的
definition_en: behaving as if you are better or more important than others

scene: 新来的主管打断了每个人的发言，眼睛只看天花板。His arrogant manner angered the whole team.
sceneCN: 这里 arrogant 是「傲慢的」（第 1 个义项：自视高人一等）；句意是他傲慢的态度激怒了整个团队。
