senses.title: Behaving superior to others
senses.definition: showing an exaggerated sense of one's own importance in dealing with people
senses.definitionCN: 待人时表现出夸大的自我重要感
senses.example: The arrogant waiter ignored our requests all evening.
senses.exampleCN: 那个傲慢的服务员整晚不理会我们的要求。
senses.why: Arrogare means to claim for oneself, so the person claims rank nobody granted.
senses.whyCN: arrogare 意为「自取」，此人自行攫取了无人授予的等级。

senses.title: Presumptuous in claims or statements
senses.definition: excessive and unwarranted, said of claims, opinions or statements
senses.definitionCN: 形容断言、观点或言论过分而无依据
senses.example: It was arrogant of him to call every rival stupid.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟说所有对手都蠢，实在狂妄。
senses.why: What one claims for oneself overreaches what is deserved.
senses.whyCN: 自取的东西超出了应得的分寸。

intro.en: Arrogant comes from Latin arrogantem, present participle of arrogare, to claim for oneself.
intro.cn: arrogant 源自拉丁语 arrogantem，即动词 arrogare（自取、擅求）的现在分词。

items.en: The root *reg- is reconstructed as to straighten, rule, source of rogare (ask).
items.cn: 重构词根 *reg- 义为「使正、统治」，是 rogare（请求）的来源（重构形式）。

items.en: Arrogare meant to claim or demand for oneself, from ad plus rogare.
items.cn: 拉丁语 arrogare 意为「为自己索求」，由 ad 加 rogare 构成。

items.en: In Roman law arrogare named the formal claiming of a person or right.
items.cn: 罗马法中 arrogare 指对人身或权利的正式认领。

items.en: Arrogant entered Middle English via Old French with the over-claiming sense.
items.cn: 14 世纪 arrogant 经古法语进入中古英语，携带「僭越自取」义。

items.en: Today arrogant is a standard term for disdainful superiority in manner.
items.cn: 现代英语中 arrogant 是形容举止居高临下的常用词。

note.en: The arrog- family is about claiming; the -ant adjective judges the claim excessive.
note.cn: arrog- 词族围绕「自取」；-ant 形容词判定这种自取过分。

entries.definition: to claim or take without right
entries.definitionCN: 僭取、擅夺，arrogant 的同根动词

entries.definition: to repeal or abolish a law
entries.definitionCN: 废除（法令），同出 rogare 词根但义为「废除」

entries.definition: having a pleasant smell
entries.definitionCN: 芳香的，词首拼写相近但词义无关

entries.definition: proud and disdainful in manner
entries.definitionCN: 倨傲轻蔑的，与 arrogant 义近而更重神情

entries.definition: excessively proud of oneself
entries.definitionCN: 自负的，侧重自我陶醉的内心

entries.definition: behaving as if superior to others
entries.definitionCN: 目空一切的，书面语色彩更浓

normalIntro.en: Break the word into ar- + rog- (ask) + -ant to see the claim.
normalIntro.cn: 把词拆成 ar- + rog-（求）+ -ant 就能看到「自取」。

normal.en: ad + rogare = to ask for oneself: claiming more than due.
normal.cn: ad + rogare ＝为自己索求：索要超出应得之物。

normal.en: The noun is arrogance: sheer arrogance.
normal.cn: 名词是 arrogance：十足的傲慢。

normal.en: Same root: arrogate (claim wrongly), abrogate (repeal).
normal.cn: 同根词：arrogate（僭取）、abrogate（废除）。

normal.en: Haughty faces, arrogant words: pair them in your mind.
normal.cn: 倨傲的神情、狂妄的言辞：脑中配对记忆。

normal.en: Arrogantly is the adverb: answer arrogantly.
normal.cn: 副词是 arrogantly：傲慢地回答。

abstract.en: Picture a man leaning back so far his chair tips.
abstract.cn: 想象一个人往后仰靠，椅子都快翻了。

abstract.en: Hear a voice that never asks a question, only issues verdicts.
abstract.cn: 聆听从不起疑、只下断语的声音。

abstract.en: See a crown placed on one's own head, uninvited.
abstract.cn: 想象一顶王冠被自己擅自戴上头。

examples.en: Her arrogant dismissal of the proposal cost the team a week.
examples.cn: 她傲慢地否决提案，让团队白费了一周。

examples.en: He grew arrogant after his first success.
examples.cn: 初次成功之后他变得自大起来。

examples.en: The arrogant tone of the letter offended the committee.
examples.cn: 信中狂妄的语气冒犯了委员会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿罗·根特」——阿罗把鼻子翘得像树根一样高，眼睛斜视众人，一副「阿罗根特」的傲慢相。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ rogare（请求）→ arrogare（自取）→ arrogantem（自取的）→ 英语 arrogant；同根词 arrogate、abrogate、prerogative。

sensesIntro.en: From self-claiming manner to unwarranted claims in speech.
sensesIntro.cn: 由自取的做派延伸到言辞中无据的断言。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a self-claimed crown nobody granted
core.cn: 核心意象：无人授予却自己戴上的一顶冠

branches.cn: 建立在自取之上的放肆

branches.en: the proud claim inviting a fall

intro.en: The Latin root rogare (ask) builds a family of claiming words.
intro.cn: 拉丁词根 rogare（请求）构成一族「索求」词。

latinIntro.en: Roman legal language kept rogare alive in verbs of formal demanding.
latinIntro.cn: 罗马法律语言使 rogare 在正式索求类动词中延续。

definition_zh: 艺术；美术；技艺；人文学科
definition_en: creative work such as painting or music, a skilled way of doing something, or the humanities
core_image: 画布上第一笔颜色落下
scene: 展厅里人不多，光线落在墙面上。She has studied art since she was a child.
sceneCN: 这里 art 是「美术」（第 1 个义项：绘画雕塑等创造性作品与活动）；句意是她从小就在学美术。

pos.zh: 名词：艺术；技艺；人文学科

senses.title: Creative work
senses.definition: painting, sculpture, music and similar forms of expression
senses.definitionCN: 绘画、雕塑、音乐等表达形式
senses.example: She has studied art since she was a child.
senses.exampleCN: 她从小就在学美术。
senses.why: Latin ars meant 'skill'; the skill of making beautiful things became the name of the things made.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ars 意为「技艺」；制作美的事物的技艺，后来成了这些事物本身的名称。

senses.title: A skilled way of doing
senses.definition: a practiced ability in some activity
senses.definitionCN: 在某种活动中练就的本领
senses.example: Letter writing is a lost art.
senses.exampleCN: 写信是一门失传的技艺。
senses.why: This is the oldest sense: any craft that requires trained skill is an art.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老的一义：任何需要训练有素的技能的手艺都叫艺术。

senses.title: The humanities
senses.definition: subjects such as history and literature, in the plural
senses.definitionCN: 历史、文学等学科，通常用复数
senses.example: He took a degree in the arts.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿的是人文学科学位。
senses.why: Medieval universities grouped the verbal and moral studies as arts, a use that still names whole faculties.
senses.whyCN: 中世纪大学把语言与伦理类学问归为「艺」，这一用法至今仍用来指整个学部。

intro.en: Art is a short Latin word for skill that widened to beauty.
intro.cn: art 是一个简短的拉丁语「技艺」词，后来扩展到美。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft, method'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技能、手艺、方法」。

items.en: The accusative artem carried the word into French.
items.cn: 宾格形式 artem 把词带入法语。

items.en: art kept the sense of trained skill.
items.cn: 法语 art 保留了「训练所得的技能」义。

items.en: English art first meant learning and craft.
items.cn: 英语 art 最初指学问与手艺。

items.en: The fine arts gave the word its modern centre.
items.cn: 美术使这个词的重心移到了今天的位置。

note.en: The look-alike group is the art family; the near-meaning group gives skill and craft.
note.cn: 形近组是 art 词族；近义组是技能与手艺。

entries.definition: a maker of art
of art or artists
clever, sometimes sly
a skilled making by hand
trained ability
planned arrangement of form

normalIntro.en: Art begins as skill and ends as beauty.
normalIntro.cn: art 从技艺开始，到美结束。

normal.en: The plural arts often means the humanities.
normal.cn: 复数 arts 常指人文学科。

normal.en: The art of doing something is a common phrase.
normal.cn: the art of 加动名词是常见说法。

normal.en: Work of art is countable and takes an article.
normal.cn: work of art 可数，前面要加冠词。

normal.en: Artful can be a warning word, meaning crafty.
normal.cn: artful 有时带贬义，意为狡黠。

normal.en: The word is one long open vowel: ART.
normal.cn: 这个词只有一个长元音：ART。

abstract.en: See a brush loaded with colour above canvas.
abstract.cn: 想象蘸满颜料的笔停在画布上方。

abstract.en: See hands shaping clay on a wheel.
abstract.cn: 想象双手在转盘上塑泥。

abstract.en: See a gallery wall lit from one side.
abstract.cn: 想象展厅墙面被一侧的光照亮。

examples.en: She has studied art since she was a child.
examples.cn: 她从小就在学美术。

examples.en: Letter writing is a lost art.
examples.cn: 写信是一门失传的技艺。

examples.en: He took a degree in the arts.
examples.cn: 他拿的是人文学科学位。

dict_mnemonic.text: art 本是「技艺」：把一件事做到有章法、有美感，就成了艺术。

root: 来自拉丁语 ars「技能、手艺」，宾格 artem 经法语 art 进入英语；由「训练所得的技艺」发展出美术、技巧与人文学科诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Skill produces beautiful things, and the name of the skill becomes the name of the faculty.
sensesIntro.cn: 技艺造出美的东西，技艺之名又成了整个学部的名称。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a first stroke of colour laid on a blank canvas.
core.cn: 核心意象：空白画布上落下的第一笔颜色。

intro.en: A Latin word of skill whose family fills the museum and the workshop.
intro.cn: 这是一个表示技艺的拉丁词，其词族遍布美术馆与作坊。

latinIntro.en: The root ars also gives artful, artifice, and artisan through French.
latinIntro.cn: 词根 ars 经法语也派生出 artful、artifice 与 artisan。

definition_zh: 人工制品（英式拼写，等于 artifact）；文物；出土器物；伪影
definition_en: the British spelling of artifact: an object made by a person, especially one of historical interest, or a false feature produced by an instrument
core_image: 同一块打制石片出现在两本图录里，一本按英式拼写，一本按美式拼写，指的都是它
scene: 英式考古报告的前言里，编辑把全文的「人工制品」一词统一成英式拼写，并在注释里说明它与美式写法指同一事物。The British editor standardises artefact throughout the report and notes that it equals the American spelling.
sceneCN: 这里 artefact 指「人工制品」这一概念本身，只是采用英式拼写（第 1 个义项：由人制作、供研究或收藏的实物）；句意为编辑把报告里的人工制品一词统一为英式写法并注明与美式同义。可辨识物件：清样稿、红笔、拼写表、注释框、校样夹。

pos.zh: 人工制品；文物；出土器物（英式拼写）
伪影；人为产物（英式拼写）

senses.title: British spelling of a made object
senses.titleCN: 人工制品：英式拼写下的同一概念
senses.definition: an object made by human skill, written with the British spelling
senses.definitionCN: 由人的技艺制作的实物，采用英式拼写
senses.example: The catalogue lists every artefact by period and material.
senses.exampleCN: 图录按年代与材质列出每一件人工制品。
senses.why: The word is the same Latin combination as artifact, arte plus factum; British orthography kept the -e- of arte, while American usage dropped it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词与 artifact 是同一个拉丁组合 arte 加 factum；英式正字保留了 arte 中的 -e-，美式则将其省略。

senses.title: An excavated find in British reports
senses.titleCN: 出土器物：英式报告中的考古发现
senses.definition: a portable object recovered from an archaeological deposit, as recorded in British field reports
senses.definitionCN: 从考古堆积中取出的手持器物，见于英式田野报告
senses.example: Each artefact was bagged with its context number.
senses.exampleCN: 每件出土器物都连同其层位编号一起装袋。
senses.why: British archaeology writes artefact where American archaeology writes artifact; the field procedure behind the word is identical.
senses.whyCN: 英式考古写作 artefact，美式考古写作 artifact；这个词背后的田野程序完全相同。

senses.title: A handling mark in a specimen
senses.titleCN: 标本上由操作留下的痕迹
senses.definition: a distortion in a prepared specimen caused by cutting, staining or handling rather than by the tissue itself
senses.definitionCN: 制备标本时由切片、染色或操作造成、而非组织本身的畸变
senses.example: The fold in the section is a preparation artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 切片上的褶皱是制备过程造成的伪影。
senses.why: In microscopy the word marks whatever the preparative steps added, and British histology reports spell that artefact.
senses.whyCN: 在显微观察中，这个词标记制备步骤添上的东西，英式组织学报告把它拼作 artefact。

senses.title: A scanning fault in medical imaging
senses.titleCN: 医学影像中的扫描伪影
senses.definition: a false signal in a scan produced by the scanner, motion or reconstruction rather than by the body
senses.definitionCN: 扫描中由机器、运动或重建产生、而非身体本身的虚假信号
senses.example: Motion during the scan produced a bright artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描时的移动产生了一处明亮伪影。
senses.why: The same false-result reading appears in British radiology writing, where artefact is the standard spelling.
senses.whyCN: 同一「假结果」读法出现在英式放射学写作中，那里 artefact 是标准拼写。

senses.title: A compression fault in audio
senses.definition: an audible impurity introduced by compression or sampling rather than present in the recording
senses.definitionCN: 由压缩或采样引入、录音中并不存在的可听杂质
senses.example: The whistle at the end is a codec artefact.
senses.exampleCN: 结尾处的啸声是编解码器造成的伪影。
senses.why: Digital signal processing borrowed the word, and British technical writing kept the artefact spelling.
senses.whyCN: 数字信号处理借用了这个词，英式技术写作保留了 artefact 拼写。

senses.title: A bias introduced by procedure
senses.definition: a result in an experiment that comes from the way the study was set up rather than from the effect being tested
senses.definitionCN: 实验中由研究设计方式产生、而非所测效应本身的结果
senses.example: The apparent effect was an artefact of the sampling method.
senses.exampleCN: 看似存在的效应其实是抽样方法造成的偏差。
senses.why: Here the word names what the procedure manufactured; the British spelling carries the abstract sense just as artifact does.
senses.whyCN: 这里这个词指流程制造出来的东西；英式拼写与 artifact 一样承载这一抽象义。

senses.title: A cultural object in a museum record
senses.titleCN: 博物馆记录中的文化器物
senses.definition: an item catalogued as cultural property, often with a recorded provenance
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化财产编目的物品，通常附有来源记录
senses.example: The museum returned the artefact to its country of origin.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆把这件文物归还给原产国。
senses.why: British institutions use artefact in provenance and repatriation files, where the object is treated as heritage rather than as evidence.
senses.whyCN: 英式机构在来源与归还档案中使用 artefact，那里物件被当作遗产而非证据。

senses.title: The made opposed to the natural
senses.titleCN: 人为之物：与自然物相对
senses.definition: anything whose form comes from human technique, used in contrast with what grows by itself
senses.definitionCN: 形态来自人的技术之物，用于与自行生长之物对照
senses.example: A hedgerow may be an artefact of centuries of grazing.
senses.exampleCN: 一条树篱可能是数百年放牧造成的人为产物。
senses.why: The widest reading survives in British writing too: skill shapes material, and the shaped result is an artefact whatever its size.
senses.whyCN: 最宽的读法在英式写作中同样存在：技艺塑造材料，被塑造的结果不论大小都是 artefact。

intro.en: Artefact is not a separate word but the British spelling of artifact, built from Latin arte, by skill, and factum, a thing made. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artefact 不是另一个词，而是 artifact 的英式拼写，由拉丁 arte「以技艺」与 factum「做成之物」构成。年代均为约数。

items.en: The ablative arte, from ars, artis, means by skill or by craft; it is the form that survived inside the British spelling.
items.cn: 夺格 arte 出自 ars（属格 artis），意为「以技艺、以手艺」；它正是英式拼写中保留下来的形式。

items.en: Factum, the supine of facere, means a thing made or done and supplies the second half of both spellings.
items.cn: factum 是 facere 的目的动名词，意为做成之物或做成之事，提供两种拼写的后半部分。

items.en: British dictionaries fixed artefact while American ones fixed artifact; the difference is spelling policy, not a difference in origin.
items.cn: 英国辞书定为 artefact，美国辞书定为 artifact；差别是正字政策，而非来源不同。

items.en: British scientific writing extended artefact to false results in imaging and experiments, exactly as American writing did with artifact.
items.cn: 英式科学写作把 artefact 扩展到成像与实验中的假结果，与美式写作对 artifact 的扩展完全平行。

items.en: Source uncertain: the exact date at which the -e- spelling became standard in Britain is not fixed by any single authority, and early printed texts show both forms.
items.cn: 来源不确定：-e- 拼写在英国成为标准的确切年代并无单一权威定论，早期印刷文本中两种形式都出现过。

note.en: The first group holds spelling variants and words from the same Latin stock; the second group holds nearby nouns for objects.
note.cn: 第一组是拼写变体与同出拉丁词干的词；第二组是邻近的物件名词。

entries.definition: The identical word in American spelling; no difference in meaning or history.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的美式拼写；意义与来历均无差别。

entries.definition: Built from the same Latin pieces but naming cleverness itself, not the object made.
entries.definitionCN: 同出拉丁成分，但指机巧本身，而不是做成的物件。

entries.definition: The British adjective meaning of or relating to an artefact; it cannot stand as the noun.
entries.definitionCN: 英式形容词，意为人工制品的或与器物有关的；不能充当名词。

entries.definition: Something that has survived from an earlier age; survival, not manufacture, is what the word stresses.
entries.definitionCN: 从更早时代留存下来的东西；这个词强调的是留存，而非制作。

entries.definition: A sample kept for examination; it need not be made by humans.
entries.definitionCN: 留作检验的样本；不一定由人制作。

entries.definition: An object as discovered in the ground, before it is cleaned and catalogued as an artefact.
entries.definitionCN: 刚在地里发现、尚未清理编目为器物的物件。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the British -e-, the shared Latin pieces, and the parallel scientific senses.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：英式拼写里的 -e-、共有的拉丁成分，以及平行的科学义。

normal.en: British artefact keeps the -e- of Latin arte, by skill; American artifact drops it.
normal.cn: 英式 artefact 保留拉丁 arte「以技艺」中的 -e-；美式 artifact 则省略。

normal.en: Both spellings are the same combination: skill plus a thing made.
normal.cn: 两种拼写都是同一个组合：技艺加做成之物。

normal.en: British field reports bag and number artefacts; American reports bag and number artifacts.
normal.cn: 英式田野报告给 artefact 装袋编号；美式报告给 artifact 装袋编号。

normal.en: The imaging sense is identical on both sides of the Atlantic: the scanner writes the artefact.
normal.cn: 大西洋两岸的成像义完全相同：伪影是扫描仪写下的。

normal.en: If a text mixes artefact and artifact, check its publisher before assuming two different things.
normal.cn: 如果一篇文章同时出现 artefact 与 artifact，先查出版方，不要以为它们指两样东西。

abstract.en: Abstractly, the two spellings show that a word can split in form while staying one in meaning.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，两种拼写说明一个词可以在形式上分家，而在意义上仍是同一个。

abstract.en: An artefact is still evidence of a hand, whatever letters we use to name it.
abstract.cn: 无论用哪套字母称呼它，人工制品仍然是手存在过的证据。

abstract.en: The false-result sense reminds us that the observer is also a maker.
abstract.cn: 假结果义提醒我们：观察者本身也是制造者。

examples.en: The report describes each artefact in the order it was recovered.
examples.cn: 报告按器物取出的顺序逐一描述。

examples.en: Reviewers asked the authors to distinguish artefact from genuine structure in the images.
examples.cn: 审稿人要求作者区分图像中的伪影与真实结构。

examples.en: British law treats an artefact of national importance as protected heritage.
examples.cn: 英国法律把具有国家重要性的文物视为受保护的遗产。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「art（艺术）+ e + fact（事实）」——英式多留一个 e，本质还是「用技艺做成的实物」→ 人工制品

root: 拉丁 arte「以技艺」（ars/artis 的夺格）+ factum「做成之物」；与 artifact 同源同义，仅拼写体系不同。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses repeat the artifact pattern in British spelling: the made object, the excavated find, the instrument's false mark, the system's byproduct and the owned heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项以英式拼写重演 artifact 的模式：人造之物、出土发现、仪器假痕、系统产物与被拥有的遗产。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one shaped stone appearing in two catalogues under two spellings.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一块被塑形的石头，以两种拼写出现在两本图录里。

branches.en: THE SAME CORE: the British spelling covers the root sense and the widest contrast with nature without changing meaning.
branches.cn: 同一核心：英式拼写覆盖根义与最宽的自然对照义，意义不变。

branches.en: FROM GROUND TO MUSEUM: a find becomes evidence in the field and heritage in the catalogue.
branches.cn: 从泥土到博物馆：发现物在田野成为证据，在图录里成为遗产。

branches.en: THE TOOL WRITES BACK: preparation and scanning add marks that the body did not produce.
branches.cn: 工具反写：制备与扫描添上身体并未产生的痕迹。

branches.en: THE CODEC'S WHISTLE: compression leaves a sound that was never recorded.
branches.cn: 编解码器的啸声：压缩留下从未被录下的声音。

branches.en: THE DESIGN'S EFFECT: a study can manufacture the very effect it claims to measure.
branches.cn: 设计的效应：研究可能制造出它声称要测量的那个效应。

intro.en: Artefact shares artifact's Latin pieces exactly, and the British spelling preserves the ablative arte more visibly.
intro.cn: artefact 与 artifact 的拉丁成分完全相同，而英式拼写更明显地保留了夺格 arte。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, artis gives the arte- half; Latin facere, factum gives the -fact half. The same two roots build art, artifice, artificial, fact, factory and manufacture.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）提供 arte- 部分；拉丁 facere、factum 提供 -fact 部分。同两个词根构成 art、artifice、artificial、fact、factory、manufacture。

items.example: Ars covered both making and cunning in Latin.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ars 兼指制作与机巧。

items.example: The phrase arte factum means made by skill.
items.exampleCN: 短语 arte factum 意为以技艺做成。

items.structure: art (English, from Latin ars via Old French)
items.example: Stone working was a high art long before writing.
items.exampleCN: 远在文字出现之前，石作已是高超技艺。

items.example: The mechanism was an artifice of great precision.
items.exampleCN: 这个机构是一件极为精密的装置。

items.meaningCN: 非自然的、由技艺制成的
items.exampleCN: 人造材料如今可以仿制石头。

items.example: Facere stands behind many English verbs in -fy.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语 -fy 动词的来源。

items.example: Factum is the source of English fact.
items.exampleCN: factum 是英语 fact 的来源。

items.meaningCN: 做过的事，后指真实之事
items.example: The fact was established by measurement.

items.meaning: a place where things are made
items.example: The factory fired clay at high temperature.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂高温烧制陶土。
他们为博物馆制造复制品。

definition_zh: 动脉；干线；命脉
definition_en: a blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart, or a main route in a transport or supply system
core_image: 一条从心脏出发、管壁厚而有弹性的血管，血液被压着向外流
scene: 医生指着造影图上那条通往心肌的血管，讲它一旦堵住会发生什么。The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
sceneCN: 这里 artery 指「动脉」（第 1 个义项：把血液从心脏送出的血管）；句意：冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。图中可辨识物件：心脏、冠状动脉、分支血管、血流箭头。

pos.zh: 动脉（把血液从心脏送出的血管）；干线；命脉（比喻主要通道或供应线）

senses.title: Vessel away from the heart
senses.titleCN: 动脉：把血从心脏送出的血管
senses.definition: a thick-walled blood vessel that carries blood away from the heart
senses.definitionCN: 把血液从心脏送出的厚壁血管
senses.example: The coronary artery supplies blood to the heart muscle itself.
senses.exampleCN: 冠状动脉为心肌本身供血。
senses.why: Greek arteria first named the windpipe; Galen later showed that these vessels carry blood, and the anatomical sense took over.
senses.whyCN: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；盖伦后来证明这类管道运送血液，解剖义由此占据主导。

senses.title: A named artery
senses.titleCN: 具名动脉：主动脉、颈动脉、冠状动脉等
senses.definition: one of the large named vessels of the body, such as the aorta or carotid
senses.definitionCN: 体内有专名的大血管，如主动脉或颈动脉
senses.example: The carotid artery was narrowed by plaque.
senses.exampleCN: 颈动脉因斑块而变窄。
senses.why: Anatomy names individual arteries because each supplies a defined region.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学为各条动脉命名，因为每条供应一个确定区域。

senses.title: Oxygen-rich blood
senses.titleCN: 动脉血：含氧较高的血液
senses.definition: in ordinary usage, the oxygenated blood carried by most arteries
senses.definitionCN: 日常用法中指大多数动脉所运的含氧血
senses.example: The artery carries bright red, oxygen-rich blood.
senses.exampleCN: 动脉运送鲜红、富氧的血液。
senses.why: Colour and oxygen came to stand for the vessel type, even though the pulmonary artery is the exception.
senses.whyCN: 颜色与含氧量被用来代表血管类型，尽管肺动脉是例外。

senses.title: Arterial disease
senses.titleCN: 动脉病变：硬化、狭窄与阻塞
senses.definition: a condition in which an artery thickens, narrows or blocks, restricting flow
senses.definitionCN: 动脉增厚、变窄或堵塞、限制血流的状况
senses.example: Peripheral artery disease makes walking painful.
senses.exampleCN: 外周动脉疾病使行走疼痛。
senses.why: Pathology attaches the vessel name to the condition, because the disease is defined by where it occurs.
senses.whyCN: 病理学把血管名称附着在病症上，因为这类疾病的定义就取决于它发生在哪里。

senses.title: A transport artery
senses.titleCN: 交通干线：城市或地区的主干道路
senses.definition: a main road or rail line that carries most of the traffic
senses.definitionCN: 承载大部分交通的主干道路或铁路线
senses.example: The new bridge became the city's main artery.
senses.exampleCN: 新桥成了这座城市的主干道。
senses.why: Engineers borrowed the bodily image: a trunk route feeds the smaller routes as an artery feeds capillaries.
senses.whyCN: 工程师借用身体意象：主干路线像动脉供养毛细血管一样供养小路。

senses.title: An economic lifeline
senses.titleCN: 经济命脉：关键的供应通道
senses.definition: a vital route or channel on which a region's economy depends
senses.definitionCN: 一个地区经济所依赖的关键路线或通道
senses.example: The strait is the artery of regional oil trade.
senses.exampleCN: 这条海峡是区域石油贸易的命脉。
senses.why: The metaphor extends from roads to flows of goods, money or energy.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻从道路扩展到货物、资金或能源的流动。

senses.title: A palpable pulse
senses.titleCN: 动脉搏动：可触摸到的跳动
senses.definition: the rhythmic beat felt where an artery lies near the skin
senses.definitionCN: 动脉靠近皮肤处可以摸到的节律性跳动
senses.example: The nurse felt the pulse in the radial artery.
senses.exampleCN: 护士在桡动脉处摸到脉搏。
senses.why: An artery lying near the skin transmits its pressure wave, so the vessel name also names the felt beat.
senses.whyCN: 靠近皮肤的动脉会把压力波传出来，因此血管名称也用来命名可触摸到的跳动。

senses.title: The branching network
senses.titleCN: 动脉分支：越分越细的供血树
senses.definition: the branching tree of arteries that spreads from the heart to the tissues
senses.definitionCN: 从心脏向组织铺开、越分越细的动脉树
senses.example: Each artery divides until it becomes an arteriole.
senses.exampleCN: 每条动脉不断分支，直到变成小动脉。
senses.why: Anatomy describes arteries as a tree, since each trunk divides into ever finer branches.
senses.whyCN: 解剖学把动脉描述成一棵树，因为每条主干都不断分成更细的枝。

senses.title: Artery as metaphor for strength
senses.titleCN: 命脉比喻：系统赖以生存的部分
senses.definition: figuratively, the part of a system without which it cannot function
senses.definitionCN: 比喻一个系统赖以运转、不可缺少的部分
senses.example: Young teachers are the artery of the school.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻教师是这所学校的命脉。
senses.why: The image of a trunk feeding the whole body extends to any component a system cannot survive without.
senses.whyCN: 主干供养全身的意象，延伸到任何系统缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery comes from Latin arteria, from Greek arteria, which first named the windpipe. The dates below are approximate.
intro.cn: artery 出自拉丁 arteria，源于希腊 arteria，后者最初指气管。以下年代均为约数。

items.en: Greek arteria named the windpipe and the air passages. The deeper origin of the word is disputed; one suggestion links ana- 'up' with terein 'to keep', but this is not established.
items.cn: 希腊 arteria 指气管与气道。这个词的更深来源有争议；一种说法把它与 ana-「向上」和 terein「守住」联系起来，但并未确立。

items.en: Galen's anatomical work distinguished arteries from veins and showed that arteries carry blood, not only air, fixing the medical sense.
items.cn: 盖伦的解剖工作把动脉与静脉区分开来，并证明动脉运送的是血而非只有气，从而固定了医学义。

items.en: Latin took arteria directly from Greek and used it for the blood vessels leading from the heart.
items.cn: 拉丁语直接从希腊语借入 arteria，用来指从心脏引出的血管。

items.en: English artery is recorded in the fourteenth century, at first in translations of medical texts.
items.cn: 英语 artery 记录于 14 世纪，最早见于医学文本的翻译。

items.en: From the seventeenth century onward the word was applied to roads, rivers and trade routes that carry the main flow of a system.
items.cn: 从 17 世纪起，这个词被用于承载系统主流的道路、河流与贸易路线。

items.en: Source uncertainty (root and first date): the Greek etymology of arteria is disputed, and the first English citation is uncertain; any deeper Indo-European form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根与首见年代）：arteria 的希腊语词源有争议，英语最早书证年代存疑；任何更深的印欧形式都属重构。

note.en: The first group holds the vessel types and same-family words that are easily confused; the second holds near-synonyms for a main route or channel.
note.cn: 第一组是血管类型与同族易混词；第二组是「主要通道」的近义词。

entries.definition: Relating to arteries, as in arterial blood; it describes, while artery names the vessel.
entries.definitionCN: 与动脉有关，如动脉血；它描述性质，artery 则命名血管。

entries.definition: A small artery that leads into capillaries; it is narrower than an artery.
entries.definitionCN: 通向毛细血管的小动脉，比动脉细。

entries.definition: A vessel carrying blood back to the heart; the artery carries it away.
entries.definitionCN: 把血送回心脏的血管；动脉则把血送出去。

entries.definition: The main artery leaving the heart; it is one particular artery, not a synonym for all arteries.
entries.definitionCN: 离开心脏的主干动脉，是某一条具体动脉，不是所有动脉的同义词。

entries.definition: Any tube carrying blood, including arteries, veins and capillaries.
entries.definitionCN: 任何运血的管道，包括动脉、静脉与毛细血管。

entries.definition: A principal route of a railway or utility network; it matches the figurative sense of artery.
entries.definitionCN: 铁路或公用设施网络的主路线，对应 artery 的比喻义。

entries.definition: A route or link on which survival depends; it stresses necessity rather than size.
entries.definitionCN: 生存所依赖的路线或联系，强调必要性而非规模。

entries.definition: A narrow passage or route between regions, often used for transport or wildlife.
entries.definitionCN: 地区之间的狭窄通道，常用于运输或野生动物迁徙。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Greek arteria first meant windpipe; anatomy later gave it to the blood vessel from the heart.
normal.cn: 希腊 arteria 最初指气管；解剖学后来把它给了从心脏引出的血管。

normal.en: The family runs arterial, arteriole, arteritis, arteriosclerosis and endarterectomy.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis、endarterectomy。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark the anatomy: coronary artery, carotid artery, pulmonary artery.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出解剖结构：冠状动脉、颈动脉、肺动脉。

normal.en: Arteries carry blood away; veins bring it back.
normal.cn: 动脉把血送出，静脉把血送回。

normal.en: A city's main road is called an artery because it feeds the smaller streets.
normal.cn: 城市主干道被称为 artery，因为它供养更小的街道。

abstract.en: Picture a thick elastic pipe leaving a pump and branching into thinner pipes.
abstract.cn: 想象一根有弹性的粗管离开泵，再分叉成更细的管子。

abstract.en: Picture a motorway feeding a whole city of small streets.
abstract.cn: 想象一条高速公路供养整座城市的小街道。

abstract.en: Picture two fingers pressed on a wrist, counting a regular beat.
abstract.cn: 想象两根手指按在手腕上，数着规律的跳动。

examples.en: The surgeon cleared the blocked coronary artery with a stent.
examples.cn: 外科医生用支架打通了堵塞的冠状动脉。

examples.en: The river is the artery of trade for the whole valley.
examples.cn: 这条河是整个河谷的贸易命脉。

examples.en: Arteries thicken and stiffen with age.
examples.cn: 动脉会随年龄增长而增厚、变硬。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「arter 管道 + y」——从心脏向外送血的管道 → artery 动脉

root: 希腊 arteria「气管；动脉」→ 拉丁 arteria → 英语 artery。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses follow one direction: blood is pushed away from the heart through a thick tube, and that tube becomes a named vessel, a diseased site, a main road, an economic lifeline, a pulse, a branching tree and finally a metaphor for a system's vital part.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项沿同一个方向展开：血液被从心脏压进一根厚管，而这根管子依次成为具名血管、病变部位、主干道路、经济命脉、可触脉搏、分叉树，最后成为系统命脉的比喻。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick elastic tube carrying blood outward from the heart.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根厚而有弹性的管子，把血液从心脏向外送出。

branches.en: THE TUBE AND THE TREE: one artery, its proper name, and the branching network it starts.
branches.cn: 管子与树：一条动脉、它的专名，以及它开启的分叉网络。

branches.en: THE OXYGEN COLOUR: bright red blood came to stand for the vessel type.
branches.cn: 含氧的颜色：鲜红的血被用来代表这类血管。

branches.en: THE BODY'S SIGNALS: disease can be seen in the wall, and health can be felt as a pulse.
branches.cn: 身体的信号：病变可见于管壁，健康可感于脉搏。

branches.en: THE METAPHOR OF ROUTES: roads and trade channels feed a region as arteries feed tissue.
branches.cn: 路线比喻：道路与贸易通道供养一个地区，正如动脉供养组织。

branches.en: THE VITAL PART: any system has a component it cannot live without.
branches.cn: 命脉部分：任何系统都有一个缺之不可的组成部分。

intro.en: Artery is a Greek noun taken into Latin with little change; its English derivatives are built on the stem arteri-.
intro.cn: artery 是几乎原样进入拉丁语的希腊名词；其英语派生词都建在词干 arteri- 上。

latinIntro.en: Greek and Latin arteria supply arterial, arteriole, arteritis and arteriosclerosis; the Greek origin is shared, and the deeper root is disputed.
latinIntro.cn: 希腊语与拉丁语 arteria 提供 arterial、arteriole、arteritis、arteriosclerosis；其希腊来源是共有的，更深词根有争议。

items.meaning: a vessel carrying blood from the heart
items.meaningCN: 把血从心脏送出的血管
items.example: The artery was cleared with a stent.
items.exampleCN: 这条动脉用支架打通了。

items.example: Giant cell arteritis affects the scalp vessels.
items.exampleCN: 巨细胞动脉炎影响头皮血管。
动脉硬化在数十年间缓慢发展。

items.meaning: surgical removal of plaque from inside an artery
items.meaningCN: 从动脉内壁切除斑块的手术
items.exampleCN: 颈动脉内膜切除术降低中风风险。

items.meaning: a main road in a transport network
items.meaningCN: 交通网络中的主干道路
items.example: The arterial road carries traffic around the city.
items.exampleCN: 这条主干道承载绕城交通。

items.meaning: the main artery from the heart
items.example: The aorta is the body's largest artery.
items.exampleCN: 主动脉是体内最大的动脉。

definition_zh: n. 关节炎（关节疼痛、肿胀与僵硬）；关节炎症的统称
definition_en: A condition in which one or more joints become painful, swollen and stiff; a general medical term for inflammation of the joints.
core_image: 手指关节又肿又硬，弯一下就疼
scene: 她手指的关节一到阴天就肿痛。Arthritis makes her finger joints swell in damp weather.
sceneCN: 第 1 个义项：arthritis 指关节发炎导致的疼痛、肿胀与僵硬。

senses.title: Inflammation of the joints
senses.definition: a disease in which joints become swollen, painful and stiff, covering many distinct conditions
senses.definitionCN: 关节肿胀、疼痛、僵硬的疾病，涵盖多种不同病症
senses.example: Arthritis of the knee made climbing stairs hard.
senses.exampleCN: 膝关节的关节炎让上楼变得困难。
senses.why: The ending -itis names inflammation, so the word itself tells you the joint is inflamed rather than merely worn.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -itis 表示炎症，所以这个词本身就在说关节「发炎」，而不只是磨损。

senses.title: The daily burden of the disease
senses.definition: the practical condition of living with stiff and painful joints, as in managing arthritis
senses.definitionCN: 带着僵硬疼痛的关节生活的实际状况，如「控制关节炎」
senses.example: She manages her arthritis with gentle daily exercise.
senses.exampleCN: 她靠每天温和的运动来控制关节炎。
senses.why: Because the condition is lifelong, the word came to name a whole routine of care rather than a single attack.
senses.whyCN: 由于这种病是长期的，这个词逐渐指整套照护日常，而不只是一次发作。

intro.en: Arthritis is Greek arthritis, from arthron, joint, plus the ending -itis, inflammation: literally inflammation of a joint.
intro.cn: arthritis 就是希腊语 arthritis，由 arthron「关节」加表示炎症的后缀 -itis 构成：字面意思就是「关节发炎」。

items.en: Greek arthron meant a joint, the fitting where two bones meet and move against each other.
items.cn: 希腊语 arthron 意为「关节」，即两块骨头相接、彼此滑动的那个接合处。

items.en: The ending -itis marked inflammation of a named part, as in bronchitis and gastritis.
items.cn: 后缀 -itis 标示某个部位的炎症，如支气管炎与胃炎。

items.en: Greek physicians already used arthritis for joint disease, joining the part to its inflammation.
items.cn: 希腊医生已用 arthritis 指关节疾病，把部位与炎症拼在一起。

items.en: Latin kept the Greek word for joint disease and passed it into medical writing across Europe.
items.cn: 拉丁语沿用了这个希腊词指关节病，并把它传进全欧洲的医学文献。

items.en: English records arthritis from the sixteenth century as a general name for painful, swollen joints.
items.cn: 英语从十六世纪起记录 arthritis，作为关节疼痛肿胀的统称。

items.en: Nineteenth-century medicine split the term into rheumatoid disease, wear of the cartilage and gout, each with its own cause.
items.cn: 十九世纪医学把这个统称拆成「类风湿」「软骨磨损」与「痛风」等类型，各有病因。

note.en: The look-alike group keeps the joint root together and adds another -itis word; the near-meaning group separates inflammation from wear and from older umbrella terms.
note.cn: 形近组把「关节」词根排在一起，并加上另一个 -itis 结尾的词；近义组把「发炎」与「磨损」以及旧的统称区分开。

entries.definition: Affected by or relating to joint inflammation.
entries.definitionCN: 患关节炎的；与关节炎有关的。

entries.definition: An animal with jointed legs and a hard shell.
entries.definitionCN: 有分节腿与硬壳的动物。

entries.definition: Looking inside a joint with a small camera.
entries.definitionCN: 用微型摄像头查看关节内部。

entries.definition: Inflammation of the appendix.
Swelling and heat in body tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 身体组织的肿胀与发热。

entries.definition: An older term for painful joints and muscles.
A painful joint disease caused by crystals.
entries.definitionCN: 结晶沉积引起的关节疼痛疾病。

entries.definition: Wear of a joint without inflammation.

normalIntro.en: Arthritis is arthr-, joint, plus -itis, inflammation: the ending tells you which part is inflamed.
normalIntro.cn: arthritis 就是 arthr-「关节」加 -itis「炎症」：后缀告诉你发炎的是哪个部位。

normal.en: The ending -itis always marks inflammation.
normal.cn: 后缀 -itis 一律表示炎症。

normal.en: Arthron is joint, so arthropod means jointed foot.
normal.cn: arthron 是关节，所以 arthropod 意为「分节的足」。

normal.en: Rheumatoid disease and cartilage wear are different conditions.
normal.cn: 类风湿与软骨磨损是不同的病。

normal.en: Arthritis is uncountable in ordinary use.
normal.cn: arthritis 在日常用法中不可数。

normal.en: Arthritic describes both a person and a joint.
normal.cn: arthritic 既可形容人，也可形容关节。

abstract.en: Picture a finger joint swollen and hard to bend.
abstract.cn: 想象一个肿胀的手指关节，难以弯曲。

abstract.en: Imagine stairs that must be taken one at a time.
abstract.cn: 想象只能一阶一阶挪上去的楼梯。

abstract.en: Think of a hinge that has rusted from the inside.
abstract.cn: 想象一个从里面锈住的合页。

examples.en: Arthritis stiffened his hands each morning.
examples.cn: 关节炎让他每天早晨双手僵硬。

examples.en: Warm water eased her arthritis.
examples.cn: 温水缓解了她的关节炎。

examples.en: The clinic treats arthritis in older patients.
examples.cn: 这家门诊治疗老年患者的关节炎。

dict_mnemonic.text: 拆件记忆：arthr-「关节」+ -itis「炎」——关节发炎，就是关节炎 arthritis。

root: 希腊语 arthron「关节」加表示炎症的后缀 -itis 构成 arthritis「关节病」，经拉丁语进入十六世纪英语；同根还有 arthropod「节肢动物」与 arthroscopy「关节镜」。

sensesIntro.en: The two senses are the same inflamed hinge seen twice: once as a diagnosis, once as the daily life built around it.
sensesIntro.cn: 两个义项是同一个「发炎的合页」被看了两遍：一次作为诊断，一次作为围绕它建立的日常生活。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger joint swollen and hard, painful to bend
core.cn: 核心意象：手指关节又肿又硬，弯一下就疼

branches.en: Stairs taken one step at a time.
branches.cn: 一阶一阶挪上去的楼梯。

branches.en: One inflamed hinge, a diagnosis and a routine.
branches.cn: 同一个发炎的合页，既是诊断也是日常。

intro.en: Arthritis is arthr-, joint, plus -itis, inflammation; the same joint root builds arthropod, arthroscopy and arthralgia.
intro.cn: arthritis 是 arthr-「关节」加 -itis「炎症」；同一「关节」词根还构成 arthropod、arthroscopy 与 arthralgia。

latinIntro.en: The medical layer is Greek arthron, joint, and -itis, inflammation; Latin articulus, a little joint, gives article and articulate beside it.
latinIntro.cn: 医学层次是希腊语 arthron「关节」与 -itis「炎症」；旁边的拉丁语 articulus「小关节」产生 article 与 articulate。

latinEntries.exampleCN: arthron 是「关节」词族的起点。
articulus 产生 article 与 articulate。

definition_zh: 节肢动物（身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的无脊椎动物）
definition_en: an invertebrate with a segmented body, a hard exoskeleton and jointed legs, such as an insect, spider or crab
core_image: 放大镜下一条分节的腿正在弯折，每个关节都像小小的折页铰链
scene: 放大镜下，观察者看见一条分节的腿在弯折，每一节都像小小的铰链。 The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint like a tiny hinge.
sceneCN: 这里 arthropod 指「节肢动物」（第 1 个义项：身体分节、具外骨骼与分节附肢的动物）；句意为这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处像小铰链一样转动。

forms.label: 复合形容词（节肢动物传播的）

senses.title: A member of the phylum Arthropoda
senses.definition: any invertebrate of the phylum Arthropoda, with a segmented body and jointed appendages
senses.definitionCN: 节肢动物门中任何身体分节、附肢也分节的无脊椎动物
senses.example: The arthropod moved its segmented leg at each joint.
senses.exampleCN: 这只节肢动物让分节的腿在每个关节处转动。
senses.why: The name is Greek for 'jointed foot', so the defining feature is written into the word itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个名字在希腊语里就是「分节的足」，因此定义特征直接写进了词里。

senses.title: The group as a whole
senses.titleCN: 作为整体的节肢动物类群
senses.definition: the arthropods collectively, the largest animal phylum
senses.definitionCN: 所有节肢动物作为一个整体，是动物界最大的门
senses.example: Arthropods make up most known animal species.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物构成了已知动物物种的大多数。
senses.why: Because the group is enormous, the plural often stands for a category rather than a set of individuals.
senses.whyCN: 由于类群极庞大，复数形式常代表一个范畴，而不是若干个体。

senses.title: Used as an attributive label
senses.titleCN: 作定语标示传播或来源
senses.definition: used before another noun to say that something is carried, caused or made by arthropods
senses.definitionCN: 放在另一名词前，表示由节肢动物携带、引起或制造
senses.example: Arthropod-borne viruses spread faster in warm, wet seasons.
senses.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的病毒在温暖潮湿的季节扩散更快。
senses.why: Public health needed a compact label for diseases carried by insects and ticks, and arthropod supplied it.
senses.whyCN: 公共卫生需要简洁标签来指昆虫与蜱类携带的疾病，arthropod 正好补上。

senses.title: A fossil arthropod
senses.definition: ancient arthropod remains, including trilobites and fossil insects
senses.definitionCN: 古代节肢动物遗骸，包括三叶虫与昆虫化石
senses.example: Trilobites are arthropods that vanished before the dinosaurs.
senses.exampleCN: 三叶虫是在恐龙之前就灭绝的节肢动物。
senses.why: The hard exoskeleton fossilizes well, making arthropods central to palaeontology.
senses.whyCN: 硬外骨骼容易形成化石，使节肢动物成为古生物学的核心对象。

senses.title: An agricultural pest
senses.definition: an arthropod that damages crops or stored food
senses.definitionCN: 损害作物或仓储食物的节肢动物
senses.example: The spray targets arthropods that feed on the leaves.
senses.exampleCN: 这种喷剂针对取食叶片的节肢动物。
senses.why: Pest control needs a word broad enough to cover insects and mites together.
senses.whyCN: 害虫防治需要一个足够宽、能同时涵盖昆虫与螨类的词。

senses.title: A disease vector
senses.definition: an arthropod that transmits a pathogen from one host to another, such as a mosquito or tick
senses.definitionCN: 把病原体从一个宿主传给另一宿主的节肢动物，如蚊或蜱
senses.example: The mosquito is the arthropod responsible for the outbreak.
senses.exampleCN: 蚊子是造成这次疫情的节肢动物媒介。
senses.why: Epidemiology uses the phylum name because the vector may be a fly, a flea or a tick.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学用门名，因为媒介可能是蝇、蚤或蜱。

senses.title: A laboratory model
senses.definition: an arthropod used in genetics or physiology, especially the fruit fly
senses.definitionCN: 用于遗传学或生理学研究的节肢动物，尤指果蝇
senses.example: The fruit fly gave arthropods a central place in genetics.
senses.exampleCN: 果蝇让节肢动物在遗传学中占据了中心位置。
senses.why: Short generations and easy breeding made one arthropod the workhorse of genetics.
senses.whyCN: 世代短、易饲养，使某一种节肢动物成了遗传学的主力。

senses.title: An introduced or invasive species
senses.titleCN: 引入或入侵的节肢动物
senses.definition: an arthropod that has spread outside its native range and disrupts ecosystems
senses.definitionCN: 扩散到原分布区之外、扰乱生态系统的节肢动物
senses.example: The introduced arthropod has no local predator.
senses.exampleCN: 这种外来节肢动物在当地没有天敌。
senses.why: Invasion biology names the group because the invader is often an insect or a crab.
senses.whyCN: 入侵生物学用类群名，因为入侵者常是昆虫或蟹类。

intro.en: Arthropod is Greek arthron 'joint' plus pous 'foot', a scientific compound that says exactly what the animal is. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: arthropod 由希腊 arthron「关节」加 pous「足」构成，这个科学复合词把动物的特征直接说了出来。年代均为约数。

items.en: Arthron meant 'joint, articulation'. It is generally connected to a root meaning 'to fit together', but that earlier form is a reconstruction.
items.cn: arthron 意为「关节、接合处」。一般认为它与意为「接合在一起」的词根有关，但那个更早的形式属重构。

items.en: Pous (stem pod-) meant 'foot', the same word behind tripod and podiatry.
items.cn: pous（词干 pod-）意为「足」，tripod 与 podiatry 也出自这个词。

items.en: The compound 'jointed foot' was coined in modern scientific Latin as Arthropoda and then borrowed into English as arthropod.
items.cn: 「分节的足」这一复合形式在近代科学拉丁语中被造为 Arthropoda，随后作为 arthropod 借入英语。

items.en: Nineteenth-century zoology fixed Arthropoda as the phylum containing insects, arachnids and crustaceans; the exact coiner and date are not settled.
items.cn: 19 世纪动物学把 Arthropoda 固定为包含昆虫、蛛形类与甲壳类的门；确切的造词者与年代尚无定论。

items.en: Twentieth-century public health and agriculture produced fixed phrases such as arthropod vector and arthropod-borne disease.
items.cn: 20 世纪的公共卫生与农业产生了 arthropod vector、arthropod-borne disease 等固定说法。

items.en: Source uncertain (details only): the Greek roots are clear, but the pre-Greek root of arthron is reconstructed and the exact first use of the English noun is approximate.
items.cn: 来源不确定（仅细节）：希腊词根清楚，但 arthron 在希腊语之前的词根属重构，英语名词的确切首见年代也只是约数。

note.en: Group one holds words from the same Greek joint-root; group two holds animal-group names that overlap with arthropods without being synonyms.
note.cn: 第一组是同出希腊「关节」词根的字词；第二组是与节肢动物重叠但并非同义的动物类群名。

entries.definition: Inflammation of a joint, built from arthron 'joint' plus -itis 'inflammation'; same root, medical meaning.
entries.definitionCN: 关节炎症，由 arthron「关节」加 -itis「炎症」构成；同词根，医学义。

entries.definition: A joint or a joint disorder, from the same Greek root; it names a body part, not an animal.
entries.definitionCN: 指关节或关节病变，同出希腊词根；它指身体部位，不指动物。

entries.definition: A prefix meaning 'joint', used in arthroscopy and arthroplasty; it is a word part, not a whole word.
entries.definitionCN: 意为「关节」的构词成分，用于 arthroscopy、arthroplasty；它是词素，不是完整单词。

entries.definition: The formal Latin name of the phylum; Arthropoda is the group, arthropod is one member.
entries.definitionCN: 该门的正式拉丁名；Arthropoda 是类群，arthropod 是其中一个成员。

entries.definition: A six-legged arthropod with three body regions; insects are a class inside Arthropoda, not the whole phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有六条腿、身体分三区的节肢动物；昆虫是节肢动物门内的一个纲，不是整个门。

entries.definition: An eight-legged arthropod such as a spider or tick; another class within the same phylum.
entries.definitionCN: 有八条腿的节肢动物，如蜘蛛或蜱；同一门内的另一个纲。

entries.definition: A shelled arthropod such as a crab; it is a major subgroup of arthropods.
entries.definitionCN: 有硬壳的节肢动物，如蟹；它是节肢动物的一个主要亚群。

entries.definition: Any animal without a backbone, including arthropods, mollusks and worms; it is broader than arthropod.
entries.definitionCN: 任何没有脊椎的动物，包括节肢动物、软体动物与蠕虫；比 arthropod 更宽。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: arthro- 'joint' + pod 'foot': the animal with jointed feet.
normal.cn: arthro-「关节」+ pod「足」：长着分节足的动物。

normal.en: Insects, spiders, crabs and centipedes are all arthropods, but each is a different subgroup.
normal.cn: 昆虫、蜘蛛、蟹、蜈蚣都是节肢动物，但各属不同亚群。

normal.en: Arthropoda is the phylum; arthropod is one member of it.
normal.cn: Arthropoda 是门；arthropod 是门中的一个成员。

normal.en: Arthropod-borne disease is the fixed public-health phrase for infections carried by insects and ticks.
normal.cn: arthropod-borne disease 是公共卫生固定说法，指昆虫与蜱类携带的感染。

normal.en: The hard exoskeleton is why arthropods fossilize so well.
normal.cn: 硬外骨骼正是节肢动物容易形成化石的原因。

abstract.en: Picture a suit of armour worn outside the body, with every limb on a hinge.
abstract.cn: 想象一套穿在身体外面的盔甲，每条肢体都装在铰链上。

abstract.en: Picture a group so numerous that it outnumbers all other animals combined.
abstract.cn: 想象一个类群，数量超过其他所有动物的总和。

abstract.en: Picture a mosquito that is both a pest and a delivery route for disease.
abstract.cn: 想象一只蚊子，既是害虫，也是疾病的投送路径。

examples.en: Arthropods account for more than half of all described animal species.
examples.cn: 节肢动物占全部已描述动物物种的一半以上。

examples.en: The trap was designed to sample small arthropods in the soil.
examples.cn: 这个陷阱用来采集土壤中的小型节肢动物。

examples.en: Arthropod vectors include mosquitoes, fleas and ticks.
examples.cn: 节肢动物媒介包括蚊、蚤与蜱。

dict_mnemonic.text: arthro（关节）+ pod（足）——关节一节一节、足也一节一节，就是节肢动物

root: 希腊 arthron「关节」+ pous（词干 pod-）「足」；arthron 的更深词源一般认为是「接合」词根，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow a jointed animal across disciplines: a phylum member, the vast group, a disease label, a fossil, a pest, a vector, a lab model and an invader.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项让一种分节动物穿过不同学科：门类成员、庞大类群、疾病标签、化石、害虫、传播媒介、实验模型与入侵者。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a segmented leg bending at each joint like a row of tiny hinges.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条分节的腿在每个关节处弯折，像一排小铰链。

branches.en: ONE AND ALL: a single jointed animal, or the largest phylum on Earth.
branches.cn: 个体与全部：单个分节动物，或地球上最大的门。

branches.en: CARRIER: the same group name labels diseases and names the vector.
branches.cn: 携带者：同一类群名既给疾病贴标签，也指传播媒介。

branches.en: DEEP TIME: hard exoskeletons make excellent fossils.
branches.cn: 深时：硬外骨骼极易形成化石。

branches.en: TROUBLE: the group includes both native pests and introduced invaders.
branches.cn: 麻烦：类群中既有本地害虫，也有外来入侵者。

branches.en: RESEARCH: short generations make one arthropod a genetic workhorse.
branches.cn: 研究：世代短，使某种节肢动物成为遗传学主力。

intro.en: Arthropod is a transparent Greek compound, and both halves recur in medical and scientific words.
intro.cn: arthropod 是透明的希腊复合词，两半都反复出现在医学与科学词汇中。

latinIntro.en: The source is Greek, not Latin; arthron and pous entered scientific Latin as Arthropoda before English borrowed the noun.
latinIntro.cn: 来源是希腊语而非拉丁语；arthron 与 pous 先进入科学拉丁语构成 Arthropoda，英语再借入该名词。

items.example: The prefix marks the jointed body.
items.exampleCN: 这个前缀标出分节的身体。

items.example: The second element marks the limbs.
Every arthropod has a segmented body.
items.exampleCN: 每只节肢动物都有分节的身体。
节肢动物遍布每一处陆地生境。

items.example: The arthropodan cuticle is stiff but flexible.
items.exampleCN: 节肢动物的角质层坚硬而有韧性。
节肢动物门是最大的门。

items.example: Arthritis shares the joint root but names a disease.
items.exampleCN: arthritis 同出「关节」词根，却指一种疾病。

items.example: Tripod uses the same foot word.

items.exampleCN: 节肢动物传播的感染在夏季增多。

latinEntries.meaningCN: 具分节足的动物（节肢动物门）

definition_zh: 文章；物品；冠词；条款
definition_en: a piece of writing in a newspaper, a single object, a word like the or a, or a clause in a document
core_image: 一份文字被分成一段一段的小节
scene: 早餐桌上摊着刚送来的报纸。She read an article about the harbour project.
sceneCN: 这里 article 是「文章」（第 1 个义项：报刊上的一篇文字）；句意是她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。

pos.zh: 名词：文章；物品；冠词；条款

derivatives.zh: 动词：清楚表达，同出 articulus 一词

senses.title: A piece of writing
senses.definition: a short piece published in a paper or magazine
senses.definitionCN: 发表在报纸或杂志上的短篇文字
senses.example: She read an article about the harbour project.
senses.exampleCN: 她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。
senses.why: Latin articulus meant 'a small joint or part'; a published piece is one part of a larger paper.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 articulus 意为「小关节、小部分」；一篇刊出的文字正是整份报纸的一个部分。

senses.title: A single item
senses.definition: one particular thing among others of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 同类事物中的某一件
senses.example: Every article of clothing was packed in paper.
senses.exampleCN: 每件衣物都用纸包好了。
senses.why: An item is a distinct part of a set, exactly what the 'small joint' image suggests.
senses.whyCN: 一件物品是整套东西中独立的一部分，正合「小关节」的形象。

senses.title: A grammatical word
senses.definition: a word such as the or a placed before a noun
senses.definitionCN: 放在名词前的小词，如 the 或 a
senses.example: English uses the article more often than Chinese does.
senses.exampleCN: 英语使用冠词的频率比汉语高。
senses.why: Old grammarians called these little words articles because each was a small joint attaching to a noun.
senses.whyCN: 古代语法学家把这些小词叫作 article，因为它们像小关节一样附着在名词上。

senses.title: A clause in a document
senses.definition: one numbered section of a treaty or law
senses.definitionCN: 条约或法律中编号的一节
senses.example: The treaty was signed under article four.
senses.exampleCN: 该条约是依据第四条签署的。
senses.why: Legal texts are divided into numbered parts, and each part is a joint of the whole document.
senses.whyCN: 法律文本被分成编号的若干部分，每一部分都是整份文件的一个关节。

intro.en: Article comes from a Latin word for a small joint.
intro.cn: article 来自一个意为「小关节」的拉丁词。

items.en: artus meant 'joint, limb'.
items.cn: artus 意为「关节、肢体」。

items.en: articulus was the diminutive, 'a little joint'.
items.cn: articulus 是其指小形式，意为「小关节」。

items.en: article meant 'a division, a clause'.
items.cn: article 意为「一个部分、一条款」。

items.en: English used it for clauses and for items.
items.cn: 英语用它指条款与物品。

items.en: Journalism gave it the sense of a published piece.
items.cn: 新闻业赋予了它「刊出文章」这一义。

note.en: The look-alike group shares the articulus root; the near-meaning group gives other words for a written piece and an item.
note.cn: 形近组共享 articulus 词根；近义组是其他表示文字篇章与单件的词。

entries.definition: pieces, plural
to express clearly
clear expression, or a joint
a short piece of writing

normalIntro.en: An article is a small part cut from something larger.
normalIntro.cn: article 就是从更大的东西上切下来的一个小部分。

normal.en: The definite article is the, the indefinite one is a.
normal.cn: 定冠词是 the，不定冠词是 a。

normal.en: An article of clothing counts single items.
normal.cn: an article of clothing 用来数单件衣物。

normal.en: Legal texts number their articles.
normal.cn: 法律文本会把条款编号。

normal.en: The verb form is articulate.
normal.cn: 其动词形式是 articulate。

normal.en: Stress the first syllable: AR-ti-cle.
normal.cn: 重音在第一个音节：AR-ti-cle。

abstract.en: See a page folded into sections.
abstract.cn: 想象一页纸被折成几段。

abstract.en: See a short word slipping in before a noun.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小词滑到名词前面。

abstract.en: See a coat laid out as one item.
abstract.cn: 想象一件外套作为单件摆着。

examples.en: She read an article about the harbour project.
examples.cn: 她读了一篇关于港口工程的报道。

examples.en: Every article of clothing was packed in paper.
examples.cn: 每件衣物都用纸包好了。

examples.cn: 该条约是依据第四条签署的。

dict_mnemonic.text: artic（关节）加 -le（小）：一个小关节，就是一节、一件、一条，也可以是一篇文章。

root: 来自拉丁语 articulus「小关节」，是 artus「关节」的指小形式；由「一段、一节」发展出条款、物品、文章与冠词诸义。

sensesIntro.en: Every sense is a joint: a part of a paper, a set, a sentence, or a law.
sensesIntro.cn: 每个义项都是一个关节：报纸的一节、一套的一件、句子的一节、法律的一条。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a long text marked off into numbered parts.
core.cn: 核心意象：一篇长文被划成若干编号的部分。

intro.en: A Latin diminutive of 'joint' that spread through law, grammar, and news.
intro.cn: 这是一个拉丁语「关节」的指小词，遍布法律、语法与新闻。

latinIntro.en: The joint root artus also gives articulate and arthritis.

definition_zh: 人工制品；文物；考古出土器物；（仪器或方法造成的）伪影、人为产物
definition_en: an object made by a person, especially one of historical or cultural interest; also a false feature produced by an instrument or method rather than by the thing being studied
core_image: 一只手把石块敲出刃口，几千年后手早已消失，那块石头还躺在土层里等人编号
scene: 考古系的学生在实验室里给一件石制小刀贴标签，标签上写着它出自哪一层土。An archaeology student labels the artifact, a small stone blade, with the layer it came from.
sceneCN: 这里 artifact 指「由人制作、具有历史或文化价值的实物」（第 1 个义项：经人手加工并作为研究或收藏对象的器物）；句意为学生给这件石制小刀贴上标明出土层位的标签。可辨识物件：石刃、标签纸、卡尺、标本盒、记录本。

pos.zh: 人工制品；文物；出土器物
伪影；人为产物；由方法造成的假象

derivatives.zh: 人工制品（英式拼写，与 artifact 同义）
人工制品的；器物层面的

senses.title: A thing made by human skill
senses.titleCN: 人工制品：人手做出的实物
senses.definition: an object shaped or made by a person rather than formed by nature
senses.definitionCN: 由人加工制作、而非自然形成的实物
senses.example: The museum displays artifacts from the bronze age.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆展出青铜时代的人工制品。
senses.why: Artifact joins ars, skill or craft, with factum, something made, so the literal reading is a thing made by skill; a natural stone becomes an artifact only after a hand has worked it.
senses.whyCN: artifact 由 ars「技艺、手艺」与 factum「做成之物」合成，字面就是「以手艺做成的东西」；天然石块要等人手加工之后才算 artifact。

senses.title: An excavated find
senses.titleCN: 出土器物：从遗址里取出的古物
senses.definition: a portable object recovered from an archaeological deposit and used to study past behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 从考古堆积中取出、用于研究过去行为的手持器物
senses.example: Fragments of pottery are the most common artifacts at the site.
senses.exampleCN: 陶片是该遗址最常见的出土器物。
senses.why: Archaeology narrows the word to what can be lifted, bagged and numbered; walls and ditches remain features, while movable things become artifacts.
senses.whyCN: 考古学把这个词收窄到能拿起、装袋、编号的物件；墙基与沟槽算遗迹，能移动的东西才叫 artifact。

senses.title: A false result from a method
senses.titleCN: 伪影：仪器或方法造成的假结果
senses.definition: a spurious feature in an observation that comes from the instrument, the sample preparation or the procedure rather than from the subject
senses.definitionCN: 观察中由仪器、样品制备或操作程序造成、并非研究对象本身的虚假特征
senses.example: The dark line on the scan is an artifact of the staining process.
senses.exampleCN: 扫描图上的那条暗线是染色过程造成的伪影。
senses.why: Once making is separated from the object, the word can also name what the procedure made: a mark the method added rather than found.
senses.whyCN: 一旦把「造」与「对象」分开，这个词也能指流程造出来的东西：图像里由方法添上、而非对象本身存在的部分。

senses.title: A digital glitch
senses.titleCN: 数字伪影：压缩或显示产生的杂点
senses.definition: a visible or audible fault introduced by compression, sampling or display rather than present in the original signal
senses.definitionCN: 由压缩、采样或显示引入、原信号中并不存在的可见或可听瑕疵
senses.example: Heavy compression left blocky artifacts around the edges.
senses.exampleCN: 过度压缩在边缘留下了方块状伪影。
senses.why: The scientific sense moved into computing unchanged: the tool chain itself leaves marks that look like part of the picture.
senses.whyCN: 科学的伪影义原样进入计算机领域：工具链自己留下的痕迹，看上去却像画面的一部分。

senses.title: A trace made by the medium
senses.titleCN: 照片上并非实物的影像
senses.definition: a mark on a photograph or film produced by the lens, the sensor or the processing rather than by the scene
senses.definitionCN: 由镜头、传感器或冲洗过程产生、并非场景中实物的影像痕迹
senses.example: The pale spot on the old print is a photographic artifact.
senses.exampleCN: 这张老照片上的浅色斑点是一处摄影伪影。
senses.why: Film and lenses have their own chemistry and geometry; dust, flare and scratches are made by the medium, so the same label fits.
senses.whyCN: 胶片与镜头有自己的化学与几何：灰尘、眩光和划痕是介质造出来的，因此用同一个标签。

senses.title: A byproduct of a system
senses.titleCN: 系统的产物：制度或设计造成的现象
senses.definition: a result that arises from the way a system is built or measured rather than from the thing it claims to describe
senses.definitionCN: 由系统的构造或测量方式产生、而非其所声称描述的对象本身的结果
senses.example: The apparent rise in cases was an artifact of the new reporting rule.
senses.exampleCN: 病例数看似上升，其实是新报告规则造成的产物。
senses.why: Abstracted from instruments, an artifact is any outcome manufactured by the frame: change the frame and the effect disappears.
senses.whyCN: 从仪器义抽象出来后，artifact 指由框架制造的任何结果：换掉框架，效应就消失。

senses.title: Cultural property in a collection
senses.titleCN: 藏品：作为文化财产被收藏的器物
senses.definition: an item held, catalogued and protected as cultural property, often subject to ownership and repatriation rules
senses.definitionCN: 作为文化财产被收藏、编目并保护、常涉及归属与归还规则的器物
senses.example: The government asked for the return of artifacts taken during the war.
senses.exampleCN: 政府要求归还战争期间被取走的文物。
senses.why: The museum and legal sense adds a claim: the object is not only made by humans but is valued as part of a heritage that can be owned.
senses.whyCN: 博物馆与法律义增加了一层主张：这件物品不仅由人制作，还被当作可被拥有的遗产来珍视。

senses.title: The made opposed to the natural
senses.titleCN: 人为之物：与自然物相对的技术造物
senses.definition: anything whose form is produced by human technique, used when contrasting the made with the grown
senses.definitionCN: 形态由人的技术产生之物，用于与自然生成之物对照
senses.example: Philosophers ask whether a city is an artifact or a natural growth.
senses.exampleCN: 哲学家追问城市是人为之物还是自然生长之物。
senses.why: This is the oldest and widest reading: the moment skill shapes material, the result belongs to the class of made things, whatever its size.
senses.whyCN: 这是最古老也最宽的读法：技艺一旦作用于材料，产物就归入「人造之物」，不论其规模大小。

intro.en: Artifact is a Latin phrase turned into one English word: arte, by skill, plus factum, a thing made. It entered English in the seventeenth century as a learned term and only later became the ordinary word for an excavated object. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: artifact 是把一个拉丁短语压成一个英语词：arte「以技艺」加 factum「做成之物」。它在十七世纪作为学术用语进入英语，后来才成为指称出土器物的常用词。年代均为约数。

items.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, meant skill, craft or technique; the ablative arte means by skill, and it is the form that appears inside artifact.
items.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）意为技艺、手艺或技术；夺格 arte 意为「以技艺」，正是出现在 artifact 里的形式。

items.en: Facere meant to make or do; its supine factum supplied both the noun thing made and the ending that builds factory, manufacture and factitious.
items.cn: facere 意为制作、做；其目的动名词 factum 既提供名词「做成之物」，也提供构成 factory、manufacture、factitious 的词尾。

items.en: The earliest English records use the word in anatomy and medicine for structures produced by disease or by technique, a sense close to the modern false-result reading.
items.cn: 最早的英语记录把它用在解剖学与医学中，指由疾病或技术造成的结构，这一用法接近现代「假结果」的读法。

items.en: From the nineteenth century the word was applied to the objects of ancient craft, and that museum sense now dominates everyday use.
items.cn: 十九世纪起，这个词被用于古代工艺的制品，这一博物馆义如今在日常使用中占主导。

items.en: American usage settled on artifact, British usage on artefact; both spellings continue the same Latin source and mean the same thing.
items.cn: 美式用法定为 artifact，英式用法定为 artefact；两种拼写都延续同一拉丁来源，意思相同。

items.en: Source uncertain: no attested Latin noun artifactus exists, so the English word is a later combination rather than a direct borrowing, and dictionaries do not name the first author who used it.
items.cn: 来源不确定：拉丁语中并无已证实的名词 artifactus，因此这个英语词属后世组合，而非直接借词；辞书也没有指出最早使用它的作者。

note.en: The first group holds words built on the same Latin stock of skill and making; the second group holds words for objects close in meaning but not made by human hands in the same sense.
note.cn: 第一组是同出拉丁「技艺与制作」词干的词；第二组是意思相近、但并非同样意义上由人手制作的物件。

entries.definition: The same word in British spelling; it is a variant, not a separate term with its own history.
entries.definitionCN: 同一个词的英式拼写，只是变体，并非另有来历的独立术语。

entries.definition: From ars plus facere as well, but it names a clever device or a trick, not the object produced.
entries.definitionCN: 同样由 ars 加 facere 构成，但它指巧妙的装置或诡计，而不是做出来的物件。

entries.definition: The adjective describing something made by skill rather than occurring naturally; it does not name a thing.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，描述由技艺而非自然生成的事物；它并不指称物件本身。

entries.definition: An object that survives from an earlier time, often valued for its age or holiness; the stress is on survival, not on being made.
entries.definitionCN: 从更早时代留存下来的物件，常因年代或神圣性受珍视；重点是「留存」，而非「被制作」。

entries.definition: An item kept as a sample of its kind for study; a specimen may be natural, while an artifact must be made.
entries.definitionCN: 作为同类样本保存以供研究的物件；样本可以是天然的，而人工制品必须由人制作。

entries.definition: Any thing that can be handled; it makes no claim about who made it or why it matters.
entries.definitionCN: 任何可拿取的物；它不主张由谁制作，也不说明为何重要。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: the two real Latin pieces, the archaeology rule, the scientific reversal and the spelling split.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：两个真实的拉丁成分、考古学的区分规则、科学义的反转，以及拼写分歧。

normal.en: ars, skill, plus factum, made: an artifact is literally a thing made by skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」加 factum「做成之物」：artifact 字面就是「以技艺做成的东西」。

normal.en: The same ars stock gives art, artifice, artificial and artifact; the same facere stock gives factory, manufacture and factitious.
normal.cn: 同出 ars 的有 art、artifice、artificial、artifact；同出 facere 的有 factory、manufacture、factitious。

normal.en: Field rule: if it can be bagged and numbered, it is an artifact; if it stays in the ground, it is a feature.
normal.cn: 田野规则：能装袋编号的叫器物；留在地里不动的叫遗迹。

normal.en: The scientific sense reverses the maker: there the instrument makes the mark, not the hand.
normal.cn: 科学义把制作者换了人：那里留下痕迹的是仪器，不是手。

normal.en: American artifact, British artefact; the meaning does not change with the spelling.
normal.cn: 美式 artifact，英式 artefact；意思不随拼写改变。

abstract.en: Abstractly, an artifact is anything a system adds to its own picture, including the distortion in the lens.
abstract.cn: 抽象地看，artifact 是任何系统添进自身图景的东西，包括镜头里的畸变。

abstract.en: Every made thing carries a signature of its maker, which is why artifacts can be read as evidence.
abstract.cn: 每一件人造之物都带着制作者的签名，正因如此器物才能被当作证据来读。

abstract.en: The word keeps asking one question: was this shaped, or did it grow?
abstract.cn: 这个词始终在追问一件事：它是被塑造的，还是自己长成的？

examples.en: Radiocarbon dating placed the artifact at about three thousand years old.
examples.cn: 放射性碳测年把这件器物的年代定在约三千年前。

examples.en: The ring around the star in the image is an optical artifact, not a real structure.
examples.cn: 图像中恒星周围的光环是光学伪影，并非真实结构。

examples.en: Researchers must separate the artifact of the measuring device from the signal they want.
examples.cn: 研究者必须把测量仪器造成的伪影与真正想要的信号区分开。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「艺术（art）+ 事实（fact）」——用艺术手艺做出来的实体 → 人工制品、文物

root: 拉丁 ars/artis「技艺」的夺格 arte「以技艺」+ factum「做成之物」（facere「制作」的目的动名词）；字面为「以技艺做成之物」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one gesture: a hand works material into a thing, and that thing is then dug up, faked by an instrument, produced by a system and finally owned as heritage.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿同一个动作展开：人手把材料做成物件，这件物件随后被挖出、被仪器伪造、被系统产出，最后被当作遗产拥有。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand shaping stone, and the shaped stone outliving the hand.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把石头打出形状，而被塑形的石头比手活得更久。

branches.en: MAKING ITSELF: craft applied to stuff is the root sense, and the broad contrast with nature is only its widest form.
branches.cn: 制作本身：技艺作用于材料是根义，与自然相对只是它最宽的形态。

branches.en: THE KEPT OBJECT: once lifted and numbered, a made thing becomes evidence, and once owned it becomes heritage.
branches.cn: 被保存的物件：被取出编号后成为证据，被拥有后成为遗产。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT MAKES TOO: the method adds a mark of its own, and the same logic explains digital faults.
branches.cn: 仪器也在制作：方法自己添上一道痕迹，同一逻辑解释了数字瑕疵。

branches.en: THE MEDIUM LEAVES TRACES: lens, film and sensor write on the image as surely as a hand writes on clay.
branches.cn: 介质留下痕迹：镜头、胶片与传感器在影像上书写，如同手在陶土上书写。

branches.en: THE FRAME INVENTS: abstracted once more, any system can manufacture an effect that vanishes when its frame is changed.
branches.cn: 框架会发明：再抽象一层，任何系统都能制造出换掉框架就消失的效应。

intro.en: Artifact is built from two Latin pieces that also build a large English family, so the word can be read morpheme by morpheme: skill plus making.
intro.cn: artifact 由两个拉丁成分构成，这两个成分还构成一大批英语词，因此可以逐语素读出：技艺加制作。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars, genitive artis, gives art, artist, artifice and artificial; Latin facere gives fact, factory, manufacture and factitious. The artifact family sits exactly where the two meet.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）衍生 art、artist、artifice、artificial；拉丁 facere 衍生 fact、factory、manufacture、factitious。artifact 一族正处在这两条线的交点上。

items.example: Ars in Latin covered both craft and cunning.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 ars 兼指手艺与机巧。

items.structure: art (English, from Latin ars through Old French)
items.meaning: the practice of skill, especially in making or expressing
items.meaningCN: 技艺的实践，尤指制作或表达上的
items.example: The art of stone working changed human history.
items.exampleCN: 石作技艺改变了人类历史。

items.structure: artifice (Latin ars + facere, a thing made by skill)
items.meaning: a clever device or a trick
items.example: The lock was an artifice of great subtlety.
items.exampleCN: 这把锁是一件极为精巧的装置。

items.meaning: made by human skill rather than occurring naturally
items.meaningCN: 由人的技艺制成而非自然生成
items.example: Artificial light changed the working day.

items.structure: facere (Latin verb, to make, to do)
items.example: Facere is the source of many English -fect and -fact words.
items.exampleCN: facere 是许多英语 -fect 与 -fact 词的来源。

items.structure: factum (Latin supine of facere, a thing made)
items.example: Factum gave English fact its earliest sense of a deed.
items.exampleCN: factum 给英语 fact 最早的「行为、事迹」义。

items.structure: fact (English, from Latin factum, a thing done)
items.meaning: something that is the case, originally a deed
items.example: The fact was recorded before any theory was proposed.
items.exampleCN: 事实在提出任何理论之前就已被记录。

items.structure: factory (Latin factorium, a place of making)
items.meaning: a building where goods are made
items.example: The factory produced pottery for the whole province.
items.exampleCN: 这家工厂为全省生产陶器。

items.meaning: to make goods, originally by hand
items.meaningCN: 制造货物，原指用手制作
items.example: They manufacture the blades from local flint.
items.exampleCN: 他们用当地燧石制造石刃。

items.meaning: artificially produced, often in a false way
items.meaningCN: 人为制造的，常带虚假意味
items.example: A factitious glow came from the treated surface.
items.exampleCN: 处理过的表面发出一种人为的光。

definition_en: made by people rather than nature, or not genuine in manner
core_image: 温室里用支架撑起来的花
scene: 花店里那束花摸起来有点硬。These flowers are artificial and never need water.
sceneCN: 这里 artificial 是「人造的」（第 1 个义项：非自然生成，由人制造）；句意是这些花是人造的，从不需要浇水。

senses.title: Made by people
senses.definition: produced by human work rather than occurring naturally
senses.definitionCN: 由人力制造而非自然生成
senses.example: These flowers are artificial and never need water.
senses.exampleCN: 这些花是人造的，从不需要浇水。
senses.why: Latin artificium meant 'craftsmanship', from ars 'skill' and facere 'to make'; the artificial is what skill makes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 artificium 意为「手艺」，由 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」构成；人造之物正是技艺所做。

senses.title: Not genuine in manner
senses.definition: put on for effect and lacking real feeling
senses.definitionCN: 为效果而装出来的，缺乏真实情感
senses.example: His artificial smile fooled no one.
senses.exampleCN: 他做作的笑容骗不了任何人。
senses.why: If a thing is made rather than grown, a feeling that is made rather than felt is artificial too.
senses.whyCN: 如果一样东西是造出来的而不是长出来的，那么装出来的而非真切感受到的情绪也是 artificial。

intro.en: Artificial belongs to the Latin family of skill and making.
intro.cn: artificial 属于拉丁语中表示技艺与制作的那一族词。

items.en: ars meant 'skill, craft'.
items.cn: ars 意为「技艺、手艺」。

items.en: facere meant 'to make, to do'.

items.en: artificium meant 'craftsmanship, a made thing'.

items.en: English artificial first meant skilfully made, then not natural.
items.cn: 英语 artificial 先指「制作精巧的」，后指「非自然的」。

note.en: The look-alike group comes from the same making root; the near-meaning group gives other words for not natural.
note.cn: 形近组同出「制作」词根；近义组是其他表示非自然的词。

root: 来自拉丁语 artificialis「由技艺制成的」，由 ars「技艺」与 facere「制作」构成；由「人工制造」引申为「不自然、做作」。

sensesIntro.en: What skill makes instead of nature grows is artificial, and so is a feeling put on.

latinIntro.cn: 制作词根 facere 也派生出 factory、effect 与 difficult。

definition_zh: 工匠；手艺人；以手工小批量制作并留名于作品的匠人
definition_en: a skilled worker who makes things by hand, usually in small quantities
core_image: 一人一炉一案，面包在掌下成形，炉门上还留着手抹的泥
scene: 清晨的作坊里，面包师把面团从木盆取出，用手掌压出气孔，再送进砖炉。An artisan marks each loaf with a small slash so buyers know whose hands made it.
sceneCN: 这里 artisan 指「以手工小批量制作、作品带个人印记的匠人」（第 6 个义项：以个人风格为标志的制作者）；句意为这位匠人在每条面包上划一道小口作记号，好让买者知道出自谁手。

pos.zh: 工匠；手艺人（可数；亦作定语，如「匠人面包」这一说法）

derivatives.zh: artisan + -al（形容词后缀）→ 手工制作的（语义偏移：从人转向产品属性）
artisan + -ship（状态）→ 匠人身份与技艺
拉丁 ars（技艺）→ 艺术（同根不同线，经古法语进入英语）
art + -ist（从事者）→ 艺术家（同根，但走的是 art 而非 artisan 这条线）
arte（技艺）+ factum（做成之物）→ 人工制品

senses.title: Skilled worker who makes by hand
senses.titleCN: 以手工制作的熟练工人
senses.definition: a person whose trade is shaping material with trained hands and tools
senses.definitionCN: 以受训的双手与工具加工材料为职业的人
senses.example: The bench was made by a local artisan from oak felled on the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 这条长凳由本地匠人用庄园里砍下的橡木制成。
senses.why: The word reaches English from Latin ars 'skill' through Italian and French, and it names the person who holds the skill rather than the skill.
senses.whyCN: 这个词经意大利语与法语从拉丁 ars「技艺」进入英语，指持有技艺的人，而不是技艺本身。

senses.title: Small-scale independent producer
senses.definition: a maker who works in a small workshop rather than a factory
senses.definitionCN: 在小作坊而非工厂里生产的制作者
senses.example: Artisans in the old quarter still sell directly from their workshops.
senses.exampleCN: 老城区的匠人至今仍在作坊门口直接售卖。
senses.why: A hand worker cannot scale like a plant, so the word carries a built-in contrast with industry.
senses.whyCN: 靠手的人无法像工厂那样扩产，因此这个词自带与工业相对的含义。

senses.title: Maker of one traditional product
senses.titleCN: 某一种传统产品的制作者
senses.definition: a maker of a particular regional good such as cheese, bread, tile or lacquer ware
senses.definitionCN: 制作某一地方性产品的人，如奶酪、面包、屋瓦或漆器
senses.example: The village artisans still fire roof tiles in a wood kiln.
senses.exampleCN: 村里的匠人仍用柴窑烧制屋瓦。
senses.why: Long practice in one product turns a general hand worker into the named maker of that product.
senses.whyCN: 长期只做一种产品，会让一般的手工者变成该产品的具名制作者。

senses.title: Guild master in a medieval town
senses.titleCN: 中世纪城镇中的行会匠师
senses.definition: in medieval towns, a master of a trade organized under a guild
senses.definitionCN: 在中世纪城镇里，隶属于行会的行业师傅
senses.example: Only artisans of the guild could sell silver within the walls.
senses.exampleCN: 只有行会中的匠人才能在城墙内出售银器。
senses.why: Guilds turned a personal skill into a licensed status, and artisan was the word for that status.
senses.whyCN: 行会把个人技艺变成受许可的身份，artisan 正是指这一身份的词。

senses.title: Worker who owns the tools
senses.definition: in economic writing, a producer who owns the means of production instead of selling only labour
senses.definitionCN: 在经济文献中，拥有生产资料而非仅出卖劳动力的生产者
senses.example: The study compares artisans who own their looms with workers who rent them.
senses.exampleCN: 这项研究比较了自有织机的匠人与租用织机的工人。
senses.why: Ownership follows from small-scale work: the person who makes the whole thing usually owns the bench.
senses.whyCN: 所有权由小规模作业而来：做完整件东西的人通常拥有那张工作台。

senses.title: Maker whose work carries a name
senses.titleCN: 作品带个人署名的制作者
senses.definition: a maker valued because individual pieces can be traced to one pair of hands
senses.definitionCN: 因单件作品可追溯到某一双手而受重视的制作者
senses.example: Collectors now pay more for pieces by named artisans than for factory sets.
senses.exampleCN: 藏家如今为有名有姓的匠人之作付的钱，比工厂成套品更多。
senses.why: Where output is not uniform, the maker becomes a brand, and the word acquires a market meaning.
senses.whyCN: 当产出并不均一时，制作者就成了品牌，这个词也随之带上市场含义。

senses.title: Deliberate maker outside manual work
senses.titleCN: 非手工领域的刻意制作者
senses.definition: a person who builds something carefully, said figuratively of writers, cooks or programmers
senses.definitionCN: 精心构建某物的人，可喻指写作者、厨师或程序员
senses.example: He calls himself an artisan of small, exact sentences.
senses.exampleCN: 他自称是一个做短小而精确句子的人。
senses.why: If the essence is care plus a signature, the material can be words or code as easily as clay.
senses.whyCN: 若核心是用心加署名，那么材料换成文字或代码，与换成黏土并无不同。

senses.title: Attributive label for handmade goods
senses.titleCN: 标示手工制品的定语用法
senses.definition: used before a noun to mark a product as hand-made and small-batch
senses.definitionCN: 置于名词前，标示产品为手工、小批量制作
senses.example: Artisan bread costs more because it is shaped and timed by hand.
senses.exampleCN: 手工面包更贵，因为它的成形与发酵都靠人手掌控。
senses.why: A noun that names a maker can stand before another noun and act as a certificate of origin.
senses.whyCN: 一个指制作者的名词可以放在另一名词前，充当产地与工艺的证明。

intro.en: Artisan is a Latin word that travelled through Italian and French before reaching English, and it keeps the workshop in view where artist keeps the studio.
intro.cn: artisan 是一个经意大利语与法语辗转进入英语的拉丁词；它眼里是作坊，而 artist 眼里是画室。

items.en: Ars, genitive artis, meant 'skill, craft, art'. It is generally connected with a Latin root for 'fitting together', reconstructed as *ar-, but that root is a reconstruction rather than a recorded form.
items.cn: ars（属格 artis）意为「技艺、手艺、艺术」。它一般与一个表「接合」的拉丁词根相联系，重构为 *ar-，但该词根是重构形式，并非有记录的形式。

items.en: Artitus 'skilled, trained in an art' is the adjective built on ars that supplies the medieval stem of the word.
items.cn: artitus「有技艺的、受过训练的」是建于 ars 之上的形容词，提供了这个词的中世纪词干。

items.en: Spoken Latin formed *artitianus 'one who works at a craft'; the suffix -ianus marks a person belonging to or practising something.
items.cn: 口语拉丁构成 *artitianus「从事某门手艺的人」；后缀 -ianus 标出属于或从事某事的人。

items.en: Italian artigiano names a craftsman or tradesman and is the immediate source of the French form.
items.cn: 意大利语 artigiano 指工匠或手艺人，是法语形式的直接来源。

items.en: French artisan entered English in the sixteenth century, bringing with it the small workshop and the guild rather than the fine-art studio.
items.cn: 法语 artisan 于十六世纪进入英语，带来的是小作坊与行会，而不是美术画室。

items.en: English keeps the handwork sense and later adds the marketing sense of small-batch goods; the shared Latin root with art and artist is real, but the words arrived by different routes.
items.cn: 英语保留了手工义，后来又添上小批量货品的市场义；它与 art、artist 共享拉丁词根，但三者是经不同路径进入英语的。

note.en: The first group holds near-identical shapes, including one famous false friend; the second holds true synonyms with different emphases.
note.cn: 第一组是外形极近的词，其中一个是有名的假朋友；第二组是侧重点不同的真同义词。

entries.definition: Nothing to do with skill: it describes a well whose water rises under its own pressure, from the old province name Artois.
entries.definitionCN: 与技艺无关：指水靠自身压力上升的自流井，来自旧地名阿图瓦。

entries.definition: A maker of art, formed on art rather than on artisan; the two words share ars but came by different routes.
entries.definitionCN: 艺术创作者，由 art 而非 artisan 构成；两词共享 ars，但路径不同。

entries.definition: The adjective from artisan, now used mostly on goods and methods: artisanal cheese, artisanal mining.
entries.definitionCN: artisan 的形容词形式，如今多用于货品与方法：手工奶酪、手工采矿。

entries.definition: Art plus a form of facere 'to make'; it means a clever trick rather than honest handwork.
entries.definitionCN: art 加 facere「做」的某种形式；指巧计，而非诚实的手工。

entries.definition: The English-born equivalent; it stresses trained skill, while artisan stresses the small workshop and the trade status.
entries.definitionCN: 本族语中的对应词，强调受训技艺，而 artisan 强调小作坊与行会身份。

entries.definition: Anyone who makes something, including machines and companies; artisan implies a person and a hand.
entries.definitionCN: 任何制作者，包括机器与公司；artisan 隐含「人」与「手」。

entries.definition: A skilled worker who also sells, often at a shop or on a round; artisan usually makes rather than serves customers.
entries.definitionCN: 既制作也售卖、常守店面或走街的熟练者；artisan 通常只做不服务于顾客。

entries.definition: A worker in metal by name; artisan is the general term that covers clay, wood, cloth and food as well.
entries.definitionCN: 名字即指金属加工者；artisan 是涵盖陶、木、布、食的通称。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real collocations and real relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而不是编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: ars 'skill' + -anus 'person concerned with': the one concerned with a skill.
normal.cn: ars「技艺」+ -anus「与…相关的人」：与某门技艺相关的那个人。

normal.en: The family runs artisan, artisanal, artisanship, and on the other line art, artist, artistic.
normal.cn: 同族词有 artisan、artisanal、artisanship，另一条线是 art、artist、artistic。

normal.en: Fixed phrases mark small-batch goods: artisan bread, artisan cheese, artisan goods.
normal.cn: 固定搭配标出小批量货品：手工面包、手工奶酪、手工艺品。

normal.en: The workshop, not the studio, separates artisan from artist.
normal.cn: 分开 artisan 与 artist 的，是作坊而不是画室。

normal.en: The false friend artesian describes water under pressure, and it comes from a place name, not from a skill.
normal.cn: 假朋友 artesian 讲的是受压的水，来自地名，与技艺无关。

abstract.en: Picture a single pair of hands in a shop so small that the door is the counter.
abstract.cn: 想象一间小到门口就是柜台、只有一双手在干的作坊。

abstract.en: Picture a loaf with a slash on top, the maker's name written in one stroke.
abstract.cn: 想象一条顶上划了一刀的面包，那一刀就是制作者的名字。

abstract.en: Picture a guild seal on a silver cup, turning skill into a legal right to sell.
abstract.cn: 想象银杯上的行会印记，把技艺变成售卖的合法权利。

examples.en: A retired engineer and a village artisan rebuilt the clock tower by hand.
examples.cn: 一位退休工程师和一位村里匠人用手工重修了钟楼。

examples.en: The shop sells only what its own artisans can finish in a week.
examples.cn: 这家店只卖自家匠人一周内能完成的东西。

examples.en: Tourism has turned cheese making from a farm task into a craft with named artisans.
examples.cn: 旅游业把做奶酪从农活变成了有具名匠人的手艺。

dict_mnemonic.text: art（技艺）+ isan（人）＝ 靠一门技艺吃饭的人；记「一双手、一间小作坊、一个名字」。

root: 拉丁 ars（属格 artis）「技艺、艺术」+ 晚期拉丁 -ianus（从事某业的人）→ 意大利 artigiano → 法语 artisan；ars 更早来源一般重构为 *ar-「接合」，属重构形式。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from a pair of hands to a market label: the hand worker, the small shop, the single product, the guild master, the owner of tools, the signed piece, the figurative maker, and the adjective on a loaf.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从一双匠人的手出发走到一个市场标签：手工者、小作坊、单一产品、行会师傅、工具所有者、署名作品、比喻中的制作者，以及写在面包上的定语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pair of hands, one bench, one product, and a mark that says who made it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一双手、一张工作台、一种产品，以及一个标明出自谁手的记号。

branches.en: FROM HAND TO SPECIALITY: general hand skill narrows into the named maker of one traditional good.
branches.cn: 从手到专精：一般的手工技艺收窄为某一传统产品的具名制作者。

branches.en: SMALL SCALE AS A LABEL: the workshop facts become a word placed on goods to certify origin.
branches.cn: 小规模成为标签：作坊里的事实变成一个放在货品上、用来证明来历的词。

branches.en: STATUS AND OWNERSHIP: the guild licenses the trade, and the small producer owns the bench.
branches.cn: 身份与所有权：行会给行业发许可，小生产者拥有那张工作台。

branches.en: SIGNATURE VALUE: when pieces differ, a name on the piece becomes the reason to pay more.
branches.cn: 署名价值：当每件作品并不相同时，作品上的名字就成了多付钱的理由。

branches.en: MATERIAL BECOMES OPTIONAL: if care and signature define the word, words and code qualify as much as clay.
branches.cn: 材料成为可选：若核心是用心与署名，文字与代码和黏土一样够格。

intro.en: Artisan is built from a Latin noun of skill plus a Latin person suffix, and both parts still build English words on their own.
intro.cn: artisan 由一个表技艺的拉丁名词加一个拉丁人称后缀构成，两部分至今都能独立构成英语词。

latinIntro.en: Latin ars supplies art, artist, artistic, artifice and inert through related forms; the person suffix -ianus supplies artisan, and the same pattern gives Italian artigiano and French artisan.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 ars 经由相关形式给出 art、artist、artistic、artifice 等词；人称后缀 -ianus 给出 artisan，同一模式也给出意大利语 artigiano 与法语 artisan。

items.example: The noun is the head of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词是整个词族的源头。

items.example: The adjective supplies the medieval stem.
items.exampleCN: 这个形容词提供了中世纪词干。

items.meaning: one who works at a craft
items.example: The spoken form is reconstructed from its descendants.
items.exampleCN: 这个口语形式是由其后续语言重构出来的。

items.structure: art (English noun from Latin ars through Old French)
items.example: The short noun keeps only the aesthetic branch.
items.exampleCN: 这个短名词只保留了审美那一支。

items.example: The studio word, not the workshop word.
items.exampleCN: 这是画室的词，不是作坊的词。

items.example: The suffix moves the word from person to product.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把词从人移到产品。

items.example: The suffix abstracts the person into a condition.
items.exampleCN: 这个后缀把人抽象成一种状态。

items.example: The compound joins skill with making.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词把技艺与制作连在一起。

items.example: The same skill is here turned toward deception.
items.exampleCN: 同样的技艺在此转向欺瞒。
